```text
1	# agent-history-hygiene
2	
3	Keep coding-agent chat transcripts and plan files committed alongside
4	the feature diff they produced, without leaking `.env` contents or API
5	keys into git history.
6	
7	| Surface | Question it answers |
8	|---|---|
9	| `find-session.sh` | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?" |
10	| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?" |
11	| `agent-commit-metadata.sh` | "Which harness/model and artifact trailers belong in it?" |
12	| `bootstrap-project.sh` | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a new repo?" |
13	| `scan-staged.sh` | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?" |
14	| `probe-specstory-redaction.py` | "What does SpecStory already redact, so we don't redo it?" |
15	| `references/remediation.md` | "I already pushed a secret — now what?" |
16	
17	The skill exists to stop three common failure modes:
18	
19	1. Agents silently **dropping** `.specstory/history/*.md` and
20	   `.claude/plans/*.md` from commits because they look like generated
21	   artifacts.
22	2. Accidental `.env` echoes inside chat transcripts that then get
23	   committed and pushed.
24	3. Reflexive `git push --force` after a leak — which doesn't actually
25	   revoke the credential and often destroys teammate work.
26	
27	## When the skill triggers
28	
29	- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "stage the plan
30	  file" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
31	- Untracked `.specstory/history/*.md` or `.claude/plans/*.md` during a
32	  `git status`.
33	- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
34	  chat history".
35	- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "bootstrap secret scanning".
36	- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" — the skill steers to
37	  the rotate-first runbook instead of a history rewrite.
38	
39	## Structure
40	
41	```
42	skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/
43	├── SKILL.md                                  # agent-facing workflow and invariants
44	├── scripts/
45	│   ├── find-session.sh                       # locate current SpecStory + Claude session
46	│   ├── stage-agent-artifacts.sh              # git-add the right artifacts
47	│   ├── agent-commit-metadata.sh               # derive staged provenance trailers
48	│   ├── bootstrap-project.sh                  # install pre-commit + gitleaks, wire the redactor
49	│   ├── probe-specstory-redaction.py          # measure SpecStory's own redaction coverage
50	│   └── scan-staged.sh                        # gitleaks wrapper with agent-friendly exit codes
51	├── references/
52	│   ├── transcript-session-discovery.md       # SpecStory / Claude session layouts
53	│   ├── pre-commit-redaction-stack.md         # layered defense design
54	│   ├── specstory-native-redaction.md         # what upstream redacts, measured
55	│   └── remediation.md                        # rotate-first leak runbook
56	└── assets/
57	    ├── artifact-dirs.txt                     # configurable list of agent artifact dirs
58	    ├── pre-commit-config.yaml.template
59	    ├── gitleaks.toml.template
60	    └── redact_secrets.py                     # run in place from the installed skill
61	```
62	
63	## Integration with chezmoi
64	
65	The skill sits on top of the user's existing chezmoi infrastructure
66	(if present):
67	
68	- `~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit` (global `core.hooksPath`) runs the
69	  repo-level `.pre-commit-config.yaml` this skill installs.
70	- `~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/redact_secrets.py` was the original
71	  upstream. `assets/redact_secrets.py` is now the source of truth and reaches
72	  consuming repos as a **pinned pre-commit hook** published from this repo's
73	  root `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` — no vendored copy to drift.
74	  `bootstrap-project.sh --from-chezmoi` still symlinks the chezmoi
75	  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml` for repos that prefer it.
76	- `~/.local/share/chezmoi/.gitleaks.toml` shares rule IDs with the
77	  skill's `gitleaks.toml.template` so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist
78	  tweaks stay portable across repos.
79	
80	For repos without chezmoi, `bootstrap-project.sh` produces a
81	self-contained stack. The redactor is **not** copied into the repo: the
82	generated `.pre-commit-config.yaml` references the hook by tag, so
83	`pre-commit autoupdate` ships fixes everywhere and the script path never
84	depends on where `npx skills` happened to install the skill.
85	
86	```yaml
87	- repo: https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills
88	  rev: ahh-v1.1.0
89	  hooks:
90	    - id: redact-agent-secrets
91	```
92	
93	`bootstrap-project.sh --migrate` converts a repo off the old vendored
94	`scripts/redact_secrets.py` layout.
95	
96	`--install-hook` refuses to run when `core.hooksPath` redirects Git away from
97	`.git/hooks/`. It exits before writing bootstrap files and tells the user to
98	integrate the hook into the configured directory or unset the override for that
99	repo; the skill never edits a global hook directory on the user's behalf.
100	
101	## Default workflow: commit feature + chat together
102	
103	```bash
104	# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is "ours".
105	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh
106	
107	# 2. Stage code, then auto-add agent artifacts.
108	git add path/to/feature.ts
109	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh
110	
111	# 3. Generate the canonical final trailer block from staged artifacts.
112	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/agent-commit-metadata.sh
113	
114	# 4. Scan secrets and validate the complete English message.
115	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh
116	bash skills/local/git-workflow/scripts/check-commit-msg.sh \
117	  --agentic --staged --file /path/to/commit-message.txt
118	
119	# 5. Commit. Pre-commit re-runs redact + gitleaks as a catch-all.
120	git commit -F /path/to/commit-message.txt
121	```
122	
123	The metadata helper reads staged blobs, not concurrently-changing working
124	files. It emits deduplicated `AI-Assisted-By: Harness (model)`,
125	`Agent-Transcript`, and conditional `Agent-Plan` trailers. Pass explicit
126	`--harness` + `--model` only when a transcript cannot prove that identity.
127	
128	## SpecStory native redaction (v2.4.0+)
129	
130	SpecStory ships its own secret redaction now, so this skill is no longer the
131	first line of defense for `.specstory/history/`.
132	
133	| Ref | What |
134	|---|---|
135	| [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) | `feat(redaction): automatically redact secrets from saved markdown history` — community PR by [@warnes](https://github.com/warnes), merged 2026-07-20 |
136	| [PR #253](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/253) | A `gofmt` CI-fix fork of #235; closed in favor of #235 |
137	| **v2.4.0** (2026-07-20) | Shipped **on by default**, via the [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset, covering local markdown **and** cloud sync |
138	| [#274](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/issues/274) (open) | Adjacent leak vector — `specstory watch` exposes the cloud auth token in its process command line |
139	
140	The merged code is not the PR's: the maintainer swapped its 11 inline regexes
141	for Betterleaks, and the PR's `extra_patterns` (custom regexes) did not survive
142	that rewrite. `[redaction] enabled` in `.specstory/cli/config.toml` — or
143	`--no-redact-secrets` — is the only knob.
144	
145	### Measured coverage
146	
147	`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py` synthesizes a Claude Code session,
148	renders it twice through `specstory sync --print` (with and without
149	`--no-redact-secrets`), and diffs per secret class. Against specstory 2.9.0,
150	over 54 class/context pairs:
151	
152	| Caught by | Pairs | Examples |
153	|---|---:|---|
154	| SpecStory | 36 | Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub PAT/OAuth/Actions, GitLab, Google, Groq, Slack, Stripe, Supabase, Linear, PEM blocks, `.env` dumps |
155	| **Ours only** | 15 | Cursor, Tailscale, Discord/Zapier/Make webhooks — plus HuggingFace, Notion, WakaTime, OpenAI project keys **in prose** |
156	| Nobody | 3 | `AKIA…` access key IDs; Telegram bot tokens in prose |
157	
158	The structural finding: Betterleaks catches several classes only in
159	`KEY=value` form, via an entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule. The same token
160	in a sentence — which is how a tool transcript actually prints one — sails
161	through. Our prefix-anchored rules don't care about surrounding syntax.
162	
163	### How the two layers stay out of each other's way
164	
165	Both write the same sentinel, `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` (SpecStory's binary
166	carries the format string `[REDACTED:%s]`), and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists
167	that shape. A transcript SpecStory already cleaned passes through the hook
168	untouched — no "files were modified by this hook", no re-`git add`, no second
169	commit.
170	
171	The redactor writes `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` instead of `sk-abc...xyz`
172	truncations, and PEM blocks become `[REDACTED:private-key]` — the exact label
173	SpecStory uses. The truncated form still appears in the console report, where a
174	fingerprint helps identify which credential to rotate. `--legacy` writes the
175	pre-2.4.0 placeholders instead; it changes only the bytes written, never what
176	is detected.
177	
178	(The related rule that a bare `PRIVATE KEY` *mention* is not key material —
179	`detect-private-key` greps for `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY` headers — is enforced
180	separately by the redactor's header-scoped matching.)
181	
182	## Post-leak discipline
183	
184	`scan-staged.sh` exit codes branch on leak state (0 clean, 10 redacted,
185	20 leaks, 30 no gitleaks). When a leak slips through:
186	
187	1. **Rotate at the provider.** The only act that revokes the
188	   credential. Links in `references/remediation.md` §1.
189	2. **Assess blast radius.** Local/unpushed? Feature branch? Main?
190	3. **Scrub only if cheap.** Amend or `reset --soft` on unpushed commits;
191	   `git filter-repo` + force-with-lease on feature branches; **never**
192	   rewrite `main`.
193	
194	The runbook explicitly forbids `git push --force` against shared
195	branches — see `references/remediation.md` §5.
196	
197	## Gotchas
198	
199	- A configured `core.hooksPath` makes `.git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg` inert.
200	  `bootstrap-project.sh --install-hook` now exits 6 instead of installing a
201	  hook that Git will never execute.
202	- Native Claude/Cursor attribution is additive. The portable minimum is the
203	  final `AI-Assisted-By` + transcript/plan block; do not invent an AI email or
204	  confuse message attribution with cryptographic signing.
205	
206	- SpecStory ≥ 2.4.0 already redacts on write — don't let the hook redo it.
207	  See [SpecStory native redaction](#specstory-native-redaction-v240) above.
208	- A bare "PRIVATE KEY" mention is not a leak; `detect-private-key` matches
209	  `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY` only. Redacting prose churned transcripts for nothing.
210	- Claude Code `plansDirectory` project-level is sometimes ignored
211	  ([issue #19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537));
212	  set at the user level (`~/.claude/settings.json`) as the default.
213	- `gitleaks protect` is deprecated since v8.19.0 — use `gitleaks git
214	  --staged`. The skill uses the modern syntax everywhere.
215	- `pre-commit install` is per-clone — each teammate (and CI) must run
216	  it for hooks to fire.
217	- Global `core.hooksPath` runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml`
218	  only if it exists; a bare repo is unprotected until bootstrap.
219	
220	## See also
221	
222	- [Source](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/agent-history-hygiene)
223	- [`project-knowledge-harness`](project-knowledge-harness.md) —
224	  complementary memory harness that references `.claude/plans/` as
225	  ephemeral scratchpads. This skill closes the loop by making sure
226	  those scratchpads actually land in git.

145	
146	`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py` 會合成一個 Claude Code session，
147	用 `specstory sync --print` 跑兩次（有 / 無 `--no-redact-secrets`），
148	再逐個 secret class 比對。對 specstory 2.9.0、共 54 組 class/context：
149

151	|---|---:|---|

153	| **只有我們** | 15 | Cursor、Tailscale、Discord/Zapier/Make webhook —— 以及 HuggingFace、Notion、WakaTime、OpenAI project key 出現在**散文**中時 |
154	| 都沒攔到 | 3 | `AKIA…` access key ID；散文中的 Telegram bot token |

157	`generic-api-key` rule 才攔得到。同一個 token 出現在句子裡 —— 而這正是工具
158	transcript 實際印出 token 的方式 —— 就會直接漏過去。我們以 prefix 錨定的
159	rule 不在乎前後語法。

161	### 兩層如何避免互相打架
162	
163	兩邊都寫同一個 sentinel：`[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`（SpecStory 的 binary 帶有
164	格式字串 `[REDACTED:%s]`），而 `.gitleaks.toml` 把這個形狀加進 allowlist。
165	SpecStory 已經清理過的 transcript 會原封不動通過 hook —— 不會出現
166	「files were modified by this hook」，不用重新 `git add`，也不用再 commit 一次。
167	
168	redactor 改寫成 `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`，不再寫 `sk-abc...xyz` 截斷形式；
169	PEM block 則變成 `[REDACTED:private-key]` —— 正好就是 SpecStory 用的標籤。
170	截斷形式仍保留在 console 報告中，那裡的指紋有助於判斷該去 rotate 哪把 key。
171	`--legacy` 會改回 2.4.0 之前的 placeholder，它只改變寫入的位元組，
172	不影響偵測到什麼。
173	
174	（另一條相關規則 —— 散文中單純提到 `PRIVATE KEY` 不算金鑰材料，
175	`detect-private-key` 找的是 `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY` 標頭 —— 由 redactor
176	以標頭為範圍的比對獨立保證。）

187	   `reset --soft`；feature branch 用 `git filter-repo` +
188	   force-with-lease；**永遠不要**改寫 `main`。

190	runbook 顯式禁止對共用 branch 做 `git push --force` —— 詳見

168	
169	def redaction_placeholder(rule_id: str) -> str:
170	    """`[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` -- what actually replaces a secret in the file.
171	
172	    The rule id names the credential type, which is what a reader needs in
173	    order to know what to rotate; keeping no bytes of the secret means the
174	    placeholder can never be re-flagged by a scanner, so a re-run is a no-op.
175	    """
176	    slug = _RULE_SLUG_RE.sub("-", rule_id or "").strip("-").lower()
177	    return f"[REDACTED:{slug or 'secret'}]"
178	
179	
180	def redact_file(file_path: Path, findings: list[dict], legacy: bool = False) -> bool:
181	    """Redact secrets in a file. Returns True if modified."""
182	    content = read_text(file_path)
183	    original = content
184	
185	    file_findings = [
186	        f for f in findings if Path(f["File"]).resolve() == file_path.resolve()
187	    ]
188	
189	    for finding in file_findings:
190	        secret = finding.get("Secret", "")
191	        if secret and secret in content:
192	            replacement = (
193	                redact_secret(secret)
194	                if legacy
195	                else redaction_placeholder(finding.get("RuleID", ""))
196	            )
197	            content = content.replace(secret, replacement)
198	
199	    if content != original:
200	        write_text(file_path, content)
201	        return True
202	    return False
203	
204	
205	def filter_by_prefixes(findings: list[dict], prefixes: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
206	    """Filter findings whose File path contains any of the given prefixes."""
207	    normalized = [p.rstrip("/") + "/" for p in prefixes]
208	    return [
209	        f
210	        for f in findings
211	        if any(p in f.get("File", "") for p in normalized)
212	    ]
213	
214	
215	# Matches actual PEM private key blocks (header … base64 body … footer).
216	_PEM_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(
217	    r"-----BEGIN[^-]*PRIVATE KEY[^-]*-----.*?-----END[^-]*PRIVATE KEY[^-]*-----",
218	    re.DOTALL,
219	)
220	
221	# The private-key *header* tokens the downstream detect-private-key hook greps
222	# for (pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks BLACKLIST, matched as plain substrings via
223	# `any(line in content for line in BLACKLIST)`). These headers — NOT the bare
224	# phrase "PRIVATE KEY" — are what actually fail a commit, so the redactor scopes
225	# to exactly them. Matching the bare phrase instead used to flag and mangle
226	# prose that merely *discusses* private keys; against a live transcript writer
227	# that re-appends the words on every diagnostic command, that never converged.
228	# See the "Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop" pitfall in
229	# SKILL.md.
230	#
231	# NOTE: the OpenVPN token is split across two adjacent string literals on
232	# purpose so THIS source file does not itself contain the contiguous BLACKLIST
233	# string — otherwise detect-private-key would flag redact_secrets.py in every
234	# repo that installs it. Do not join them back together.
235	_PRIVATE_KEY_HEADER_RE = re.compile(
236	    r"BEGIN [A-Z0-9 ]*PRIVATE KEY"      # RSA/DSA/EC/OPENSSH/PGP/ENCRYPTED/SSH2/plain
237	    r"|PuTTY-User-Key-File-\d"
238	    r"|BEGIN OpenVPN " r"Static key V1"
239	)
240	
241	
242	def find_private_key_files(files: list[Path]) -> dict[Path, list[str]]:
243	    """Find files containing private-key material. Returns {path: [descriptions]}.
244	
245	    Only real key indicators count: a full PEM block, or a stray key *header*
246	    token (a truncated key, or a header quoted in prose) that the downstream
247	    detect-private-key hook would grep for. Bare "PRIVATE KEY" prose is
248	    deliberately ignored — detect-private-key ignores it too, and flagging it
249	    caused a non-converging redact loop.
250	    """
251	    results: dict[Path, list[str]] = {}
252	    for path in files:
253	        if not path.is_file() or path.suffix != ".md":
254	            continue
255	        try:
256	            content = read_text(path)
257	        except OSError:
258	            continue
259	        matches = []
260	        pem_blocks = _PEM_BLOCK_RE.findall(content)
261	        if pem_blocks:
262	            matches.append(f"{len(pem_blocks)} PEM private key block(s)")
263	        # Count header tokens OUTSIDE full PEM blocks (which are handled above):
264	        # truncated keys, or a header quoted in prose.
265	        without_pem = _PEM_BLOCK_RE.sub("", content)
266	        header_count = len(_PRIVATE_KEY_HEADER_RE.findall(without_pem))
267	        if header_count:
268	            matches.append(f"{header_count} private-key header(s)")
269	        if matches:
270	            results[path] = matches
271	    return results
272	
273	
274	def redact_private_keys(file_path: Path, legacy: bool = False) -> bool:
275	    """Redact private-key material in a file. Returns True if modified.
276	
277	    Scrubs full PEM blocks and any stray key *header* tokens — exactly what the
278	    detect-private-key hook greps for. The bare phrase "PRIVATE KEY" in prose is
279	    left untouched on purpose: redacting it mangled legitimate text and never
280	    converged against a live transcript writer. Both placeholders contain
281	    neither a header token nor the bare phrase, so a re-run is a no-op --
282	    `[REDACTED:private-key]` is lowercase, while the header regex matches only
283	    uppercase `BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY`. `[REDACTED:private-key]` is also the
284	    exact label SpecStory emits for this class.
285	    """
286	    content = read_text(file_path)
287	    original = content
288	    pem_placeholder = (
289	        "[REDACTED PEM PRIVKEY BLOCK]" if legacy else "[REDACTED:private-key]"
290	    )
291	    header_placeholder = (
292	        "[REDACTED PRIVKEY HEADER]" if legacy else "[REDACTED:private-key-header]"
293	    )
294	    # Full PEM blocks first (header + body + footer).
295	    content = _PEM_BLOCK_RE.sub(pem_placeholder, content)
296	    # Any remaining stray header tokens (truncated keys / headers quoted in
297	    # prose) -- these alone would still trip detect-private-key.
298	    content = _PRIVATE_KEY_HEADER_RE.sub(header_placeholder, content)
299	    if content != original:
300	        write_text(file_path, content)
301	        return True
302	    return False
303	
304	
305	def main():
306	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
307	        description=(
308	            "Check/redact secrets in agent artifact directories "
309	            "(specstory history + coding agent plan dirs)."
310	        )
311	    )
312	    parser.add_argument(
313	        "--fix", action="store_true", help="Auto-redact secrets and re-stage files"
314	    )
315	    parser.add_argument(
316	        "--working-dir",
317	        action="store_true",
318	        help="Scan working directory instead of staged files (default: scan staged)",
319	    )
320	    parser.add_argument(
321	        "--legacy",
322	        action="store_true",
323	        help=(
324	            "Write the pre-2.4.0 placeholders (`sk-abc...xyz` truncation, "
325	            "`[REDACTED PEM PRIVKEY BLOCK]`) instead of the `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` "
326	            "sentinel shared with SpecStory's native redaction. Detection is "
327	            "unchanged; only the bytes written differ."
328	        ),
329	    )
330	    parser.add_argument(
331	        "--paths",
332	        nargs="+",
333	        default=DEFAULT_PATHS,
334	        metavar="PREFIX",
335	        help=(
336	            "Path prefixes to scan. Default: "
337	            + " ".join(DEFAULT_PATHS)
338	        ),
339	    )
340	    args = parser.parse_args()
341	
342	    prefixes = [p.rstrip("/") for p in args.paths]
343	    existing_prefixes = [p for p in prefixes if Path(p).exists()]
344	    missing_prefixes = [p for p in prefixes if not Path(p).exists()]
345	
346	    for p in missing_prefixes:
347	        print(f"Skipping missing path: {p}/")
348	
349	    if not existing_prefixes:
350	        print("No target directories found; nothing to scan.")
351	        return 0
352	
353	    prefix_list_str = ", ".join(f"{p}/" for p in existing_prefixes)
354	
355	    # --- Detect gitleaks secrets ---
356	    if args.working_dir:
357	        print(f"Scanning working directory: {prefix_list_str}")
358	        findings: list[dict] = []
359	        for p in existing_prefixes:
360	            findings.extend(run_gitleaks_workdir(p))
361	    else:
362	        print(f"Scanning staged files under: {prefix_list_str}")
363	        all_findings = run_gitleaks_staged()
364	        findings = filter_by_prefixes(all_findings, existing_prefixes)
365	
366	    has_issues = False
367	
368	    if findings:
369	        has_issues = True
370	        print(f"\nFound {len(findings)} potential secret(s):\n")
371	
372	        # Group by file
373	        by_file: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
374	        for f in findings:
375	            file_path = f["File"]
376	            by_file.setdefault(file_path, []).append(f)
377	
378	        for file_path, file_findings in by_file.items():
379	            print(f"  {file_path}:")

381	                rule = finding.get("RuleID", "unknown")

383	                line = finding.get("StartLine", "?")

388	        by_file = {}
389	
390	    # --- Detect private key patterns ---
391	    if args.working_dir:
392	        scan_files: list[Path] = []
393	        for p in existing_prefixes:

395	    else:
396	        result = subprocess.run(
397	            ["git", "diff", "--cached", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=ACM"],
398	            capture_output=True,

400	        )
401	        staged_md = [
402	            Path(f)

404	            if f.endswith(".md")
405	            and any(f.startswith(p + "/") for p in existing_prefixes)

407	        scan_files = staged_md
408	
409	    pk_files = find_private_key_files(scan_files)

413	        for path, descriptions in pk_files.items():

421	        return 0

1	# Pre-commit hooks for a project bootstrapped by agent-history-hygiene.
2	#
3	# Installed by `bootstrap-project.sh`. The redact-agent-secrets hook is a
4	# PINNED REMOTE hook provided by the agent-skills repo -- fixes propagate with
5	# `pre-commit autoupdate` (bumps the `rev:` below), so there is no vendored
6	# scripts/redact_secrets.py to drift out of date.
7	#
8	# artifact-dirs.txt still feeds the gitleaks allowlist (.gitleaks.toml) and
9	# stage-agent-artifacts.sh; the redact hook's own `files:` default lives in the
10	# hook repo's .pre-commit-hooks.yaml (override here only if you must).
11	#
12	# See https://pre-commit.com
13	
14	repos:
15	  # Auto-redact leaked secrets in agent artifacts BEFORE gitleaks runs.
16	  # If a file is rewritten pre-commit surfaces "files were modified by this
17	  # hook" and you `git add` + recommit -- same UX as end-of-file-fixer.
18	  - repo: https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills
19	    rev: ahh-v1.1.0
20	    hooks:
21	      - id: redact-agent-secrets
22	        # Override the default artifact-dir scope only if needed, e.g.:
23	        # files: ^(\.specstory/history|\.claude/plans|\.cursor/plans|\.cursor/rules|\.opencode/plans|\.specify|\.codex)/.*\.md$
24	
25	  # Gitleaks -- block commit when unallowlisted secrets are detected.
26	  - repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
27	    rev: v8.22.1
28	    hooks:
29	      # Prefer system-installed gitleaks to avoid Go toolchain build issues.
30	      - id: gitleaks-system
31	        pass_filenames: false
32	
33	  # Standard pre-commit hygiene. Feel free to trim per project needs.
34	  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
35	    rev: v5.0.0
36	    hooks:
37	      - id: detect-private-key
38	        # This hook honours neither `gitleaks:allow` markers nor
39	        # .github/secret_scanning.yml -- it greps for `BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY`
40	        # as a plain substring. agent-history-hygiene's installed test suite
41	        # carries those headers on purpose, so exclude that one directory.
42	        exclude: ^\.(agents|claude)/skills/agent-history-hygiene/tests/
43	      - id: check-added-large-files
44	        args: ['--maxkb=2048']
45	      - id: check-merge-conflict
46	      - id: end-of-file-fixer
47	        exclude: ^\.specstory/
48	      - id: trailing-whitespace
49	        args: [--markdown-linebreak-ext=md]
50	        exclude: ^\.specstory/
51

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# find-session.sh — resolve the current agent session files for $PWD.
3	#
4	# Returns the SpecStory transcript path + Claude Code session UUID/JSONL
5	# path for the current working directory, so the calling agent can stage
6	# the right artifacts before a commit.
7	#
8	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
9	
10	set -euo pipefail
11	
12	usage() {
13	  cat <<'EOF'
14	Usage: find-session.sh [OPTIONS]
15	
16	Discover the agent session files associated with $PWD. Heuristics:
17	  - SpecStory: newest *.md under ./.specstory/history/
18	  - Claude Code: newest *.jsonl under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/ where
19	                 <slug> is $PWD with '/' -> '-' (Claude's own convention).
20	
21	Options:
22	  --format=VALUE     one of: specstory, claude, both (default: both)
23	  --json             Emit JSON instead of TSV.
24	  --quiet            Suppress stderr diagnostics on empty results.
25	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
26	
27	Output (TSV, one key/value per line):
28	  specstory_path       <abs path or empty>
29	  claude_session_uuid  <uuid or empty>
30	  claude_jsonl_path    <abs path or empty>
31	
32	Exit codes:
33	  0  always (never fails the pipeline; empty values signal absence).
34	  1  invalid arguments.
35	EOF
36	}
37	
38	log()  { [ "$QUIET" = "1" ] || printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
39	warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
40	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
41	
42	FORMAT="both"
43	OUT_JSON=0
44	QUIET=0
45	
46	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
47	  case "$1" in
48	    --format=*) FORMAT="${1#--format=}"; shift ;;
49	    --format)   FORMAT="${2:-both}"; shift 2 ;;
50	    --json)     OUT_JSON=1; shift ;;
51	    --quiet)    QUIET=1; shift ;;
52	    --help|-h)  usage; exit 0 ;;
53	    -*)         die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
54	    *)          die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
55	  esac
56	done
57	
58	case "$FORMAT" in
59	  both|specstory|claude) ;;
60	  *) die "invalid --format: $FORMAT (expected both|specstory|claude)" 1 ;;
61	esac
62	
63	# Claude's project slug: absolute $PWD with every NON-ALPHANUMERIC character
64	# replaced by '-' -- not just '/'.
65	#   /Volumes/Data/x          -> -Volumes-Data-x
66	#   /home/u/.local/share/foo -> -home-u--local-share-foo   (the dot collapses)
67	# The leading dash is intentional -- it mirrors how Claude Code names the
68	# subdirectory under ~/.claude/projects/. Using `tr '/' '-'` here silently
69	# returns an empty result for any path containing '.', '_' or a space.
70	cwd_slug() {
71	  printf '%s' "$PWD" | sed 's|[^A-Za-z0-9]|-|g'
72	}
73	
74	newest_file() {
75	  # newest_file <dir> <glob>
76	  # Prints the newest matching file by mtime, or empty if none.
77	  local dir="$1" glob="$2"
78	  [ -d "$dir" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
79	  # stat -f on macOS, stat -c on Linux — use find+sort for portability.
80	  local found
81	  found=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$glob" -print0 2>/dev/null \
82	    | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null \
83	    | head -n 1)
84	  printf '%s' "$found"
85	}
86	
87	SPECSTORY_PATH=""
88	CLAUDE_JSONL=""
89	CLAUDE_UUID=""
90	
91	if [ "$FORMAT" = "both" ] || [ "$FORMAT" = "specstory" ]; then
92	  candidate=$(newest_file "$PWD/.specstory/history" "*.md")
93	  if [ -n "$candidate" ]; then
94	    SPECSTORY_PATH="$candidate"
95	  else
96	    log "no .specstory/history/*.md under $PWD"
97	  fi
98	fi
99	
100	if [ "$FORMAT" = "both" ] || [ "$FORMAT" = "claude" ]; then
101	  slug=$(cwd_slug)
102	  proj_dir="$HOME/.claude/projects/$slug"
103	  candidate=$(newest_file "$proj_dir" "*.jsonl")
104	  if [ -n "$candidate" ]; then
105	    CLAUDE_JSONL="$candidate"
106	    CLAUDE_UUID=$(basename "$candidate" .jsonl)
107	  else
108	    log "no ~/.claude/projects/$slug/*.jsonl (slug derived from PWD)"
109	  fi
110	fi
111	
112	if [ "$OUT_JSON" = "1" ]; then
113	  # Hand-rolled JSON keeps us dependency-free (no jq/python requirement).
114	  printf '{"specstory_path":"%s","claude_session_uuid":"%s","claude_jsonl_path":"%s"}\n' \
115	    "$SPECSTORY_PATH" "$CLAUDE_UUID" "$CLAUDE_JSONL"
116	else
117	  printf 'specstory_path\t%s\n' "$SPECSTORY_PATH"
118	  printf 'claude_session_uuid\t%s\n' "$CLAUDE_UUID"
119	  printf 'claude_jsonl_path\t%s\n' "$CLAUDE_JSONL"
120	fi

2	# stage-agent-artifacts.sh — git-add agent chat + plan artifacts before
3	# the next commit.
4	#
5	# Default behavior: stage every dirty *.md under each directory in
6	# assets/artifact-dirs.txt, plus the current SpecStory transcript.
7	#
8	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
9	
10	set -euo pipefail
11	
12	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
13	SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
14	DEFAULT_DIRS_FILE="$SKILL_DIR/assets/artifact-dirs.txt"
15	
16	usage() {
17	  cat <<'EOF'
18	Usage: stage-agent-artifacts.sh [OPTIONS]
19	
20	Stage agent artifact files (SpecStory transcripts, .claude/plans/*.md, etc.)
21	for the next commit. Must be run from inside a git repo.
22	
23	Options:
24	  --session-only        Only stage the current SpecStory transcript + newest
25	                        plan file; skip .cursor/, .opencode/, etc.
26	  --include-all-plans   Also re-add already-tracked plan/transcript files
27	                        that were modified (default: only unstaged files).
28	  --dirs-file PATH      Override the default artifact-dirs.txt location.
29	  --dry-run             Print the files that would be staged, but don't stage.
30	  --allow-empty         Stage artifacts even when HEAD has no code changes
31	                        (default: refuse — prevents "commit just transcript").
32	  --help, -h            Show this help and exit.
33	
34	Exit codes:
35	  0  success (one or more artifacts staged or already clean)
36	  1  invalid arguments
37	  2  not inside a git repo
38	  3  no code changes AND no dirty artifacts (suggests nothing to commit)
39	  4  refused: code is clean but artifacts are dirty (use --allow-empty)
40	EOF
41	}
42	
43	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
44	warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
45	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
46	
47	SESSION_ONLY=0
48	INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS=0
49	DIRS_FILE="$DEFAULT_DIRS_FILE"
50	DRY_RUN=0
51	ALLOW_EMPTY=0
52	
53	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
54	  case "$1" in
55	    --session-only)       SESSION_ONLY=1; shift ;;
56	    --include-all-plans)  INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS=1; shift ;;
57	    --dirs-file)          DIRS_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
58	    --dirs-file=*)        DIRS_FILE="${1#--dirs-file=}"; shift ;;
59	    --dry-run)            DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
60	    --allow-empty)        ALLOW_EMPTY=1; shift ;;
61	    --help|-h)            usage; exit 0 ;;
62	    -*)                   die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
63	    *)                    die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
64	  esac
65	done
66	
67	# Must be in a git repo.
68	if ! git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
69	  die "not inside a git repo" 2
70	fi
71	REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
72	cd "$REPO_ROOT"
73	
74	# Read artifact dirs from the config file.
75	if [ ! -f "$DIRS_FILE" ]; then
76	  die "artifact-dirs.txt not found: $DIRS_FILE" 1
77	fi
78	
79	ARTIFACT_DIRS=()
80	while IFS= read -r line; do
81	  # Strip comments and whitespace.
82	  line="${line%%#*}"
83	  line="$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')"
84	  [ -n "$line" ] && ARTIFACT_DIRS+=("$line")
85	done < "$DIRS_FILE"
86	
87	# Warn if any artifact dir is silently gitignored.
88	check_ignored() {
89	  local dir="$1"
90	  # `git check-ignore` exits 0 if the path matches an ignore rule.
91	  if [ -e "$dir" ] && git check-ignore -q "$dir" 2>/dev/null; then
92	    warn "$dir is gitignored — staged files under it won't actually be committed"
93	  fi
94	}
95	
96	# Resolve the "current session" artifacts for --session-only.
97	find_current_specstory() {
98	  "$SCRIPT_DIR/find-session.sh" --quiet --format=specstory 2>/dev/null \
99	    | awk -F'\t' '$1=="specstory_path"{print $2}'
100	}

104	    | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null | head -n 1
105	}
106	
107	# List dirty artifact files across the configured dirs.
108	# Returns null-separated paths on stdout.
109	list_dirty_artifacts() {
110	  local dir path git_status
111	  for dir in "${ARTIFACT_DIRS[@]}"; do
112	    [ -e "$dir" ] || continue
113	    check_ignored "$dir"
114	    # Include untracked (??) and modified (M/A) entries. `-z` → NUL separated.
115	    while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
116	      # porcelain -z format: XY<space>path[\0orig_path]
117	      # We only want the path portion.
118	      git_status="${entry:0:2}"
119	      path="${entry:3}"
120	      case "$path" in
121	        *.md) ;;
122	        *) continue ;;
123	      esac
124	      case "$git_status" in
125	        "??") printf '%s\0' "$path" ;;
126	        " M"|"MM"|"AM"|"AD"|"A ") printf '%s\0' "$path" ;;
127	        "M "|"A ")
128	          # Already staged — only re-add if --include-all-plans.
129	          [ "$INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS" = "1" ] && printf '%s\0' "$path"
130	          ;;
131	      esac
132	    done < <(git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall -- "$dir" 2>/dev/null || true)
133	  done
134	}
135

137	STAGED_COUNT=0
138	CANDIDATES=()
139	
140	if [ "$SESSION_ONLY" = "1" ]; then
141	  specstory=$(find_current_specstory)
142	  plan=$(find_current_plan)
143	  [ -n "$specstory" ] && [ -f "$specstory" ] && CANDIDATES+=("$specstory")
144	  [ -n "$plan" ] && [ -f "$plan" ] && CANDIDATES+=("$plan")
145	else

147	  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do

153	# Non-artifact dirty files (staged or unstaged) mean the agent is committing
154	# a real feature alongside the transcript — that's the intended use.
155	has_code_changes() {

158	    [ -z "$line" ] && continue
159	    path="${line:3}"
160	    in_artifact=0

164	      esac
165	    done
166	    [ "$in_artifact" = "0" ] && any=1
167	  done < <(git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain=v1 2>/dev/null)
168	  [ "$any" = "1" ]
169	}
170	
171	if [ "${#CANDIDATES[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
172	  if has_code_changes; then
173	    log "No agent artifacts to stage; code changes present — nothing to do."
174	    exit 0
175	  fi
176	  log "Nothing to stage: no code changes and no dirty artifacts."
177	  exit 3
178	fi
179	
180	if [ "$ALLOW_EMPTY" = "0" ] && ! has_code_changes; then
181	  log "Refusing: artifacts are dirty but no code changes staged."
182	  log "         A transcript/plan commit without a feature diff is usually wrong."
183	  log "         Re-run with --allow-empty if you really want to commit artifacts alone."
184	  exit 4
185	fi

194	  fi
195	  STAGED_COUNT=$((STAGED_COUNT + 1))

26	dim()   { printf '\033[2m%s\033[0m' "$*"; }
27	
28	pass() {
29	  PASS_COUNT=$((PASS_COUNT + 1))
30	  printf '  %s %s\n' "$(green PASS)" "$1"
31	}
32	fail() {
33	  FAIL_COUNT=$((FAIL_COUNT + 1))
34	  printf '  %s %s\n' "$(red FAIL)" "$1"
35	  FAIL_LOG="${FAIL_LOG}FAIL: $1\n"
36	}
37	
38	# make_repo — spin up an isolated tmp repo with an initial commit.
39	# Prints the path to stdout.
40	make_repo() {
41	  local d
42	  d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/test-scan-staged.XXXXXX)
43	  git -C "$d" init -q -b main
44	  git -C "$d" -c user.email=test@example.com -c user.name=test \
45	      commit -q --allow-empty -m init
46	  printf '%s' "$d"
47	}

49	# Copy fixture + stage it under the given relative path. Strips the inline
50	# `<!-- gitleaks:allow -->` marker so the rules still fire in the throwaway repo
51	# (byte-identical to the fixture otherwise). Line-based sed → newline never
52	# enters the pattern space, so [[:space:]]* only eats the horizontal separator.
53	stage_fixture() {
54	  local repo="$1" fixture="$2" dest_rel="$3"
55	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$repo/$dest_rel")"
56	  sed 's/[[:space:]]*<!-- *gitleaks:allow *-->//g' "$FIXTURES/$fixture" > "$repo/$dest_rel"

17	  Each filename encodes its expected behavior (e.g. `real_anthropic.md`
18	  should fire, `example_shapes.md` should be allowlisted when staged
19	  inside an agent-artifact directory).
20	- `conftest.py` — shared pytest fixtures; loads the PEP 723 script
21	  `assets/redact_secrets.py` as an importable module.
22	- `test_redact_secrets.py` — unit tests for pure functions in the
23	  redactor (`redact_secret`, `filter_by_prefixes`,
24	  `find_private_key_files`, `redact_file`, `redact_private_keys`).
25	- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus tests: stages each fixture
26	  in a throwaway git repo and asserts `gitleaks git --staged` returns
27	  the expected findings (or lack thereof). Skipped if `gitleaks` is
28	  not on `PATH`.
29	- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
30	  `scripts/scan-staged.sh`: `0` clean, `20` leak, `30` missing
31	  gitleaks, `2` not a git repo.
32	- `test_bootstrap_project.py` — verifies precise, idempotent nested SpecStory
33	  ignores; confirms `history/` stays visible; checks dry-run and the explicit
34	  `--untrack-specstory-state` migration contract.
35	
36	## Test-vector hygiene (why the fixtures carry `gitleaks:allow`)
37	
38	The firing fixtures (`real_anthropic.md`, `real_openai.md`, `private_key.md`,
39	`webhook_urls.md`) hold deliberately-fake test vectors. Most use realistic
40	secret shapes plus an inline marker so a repo-root, downstream, or
41	`npx skills add`-installed gitleaks scan **skips them by default**:
42	
43	```
44	<SECRET> <!-- gitleaks:allow -->                      # markdown fixtures
45	"-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\n"  # gitleaks:allow  # test_redact_secrets.py
46	```
47	
48	The Stripe webhook fixture is stricter: GitHub's provider-level scanner does
49	not honour gitleaks markers, so its source uses
50	`__SYNTHETIC_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET__`. The corpus test expands that placeholder
51	inside its throwaway repo. The other corpus + shell tests **strip the marker
52	before staging** (`_GITLEAKS_MARKER_RE` in `test_gitleaks_corpus.py`; the `sed`
53	in `stage_fixture` in `test_scan_staged.sh`), so the secret bytes have the exact
54	shape the rules expect and the assertions still fire. Principle: **fake test
55	vectors are out of scan scope by default, and only "fire" when a test re-plants
56	them.**
57	
58	Invariant — **the strip must be byte-identical**: never change a secret's length
59	or the length-sensitive rules (`sk-proj-…{80,}`, `sk-ant-api\d{2}-…{93}AA`, the
60	webhook regexes) stop matching. When adding a new firing fixture, append the
61	marker with a single leading space (`<SECRET> <!-- gitleaks:allow -->`); the
62	strip regex reclaims exactly that separator. `clean.md` / `example_shapes.md`
63	carry no marker (the strip is a no-op) and must keep their must-not-fire
64	behavior. GitHub-native secret scanning ignores the marker; it's excluded
65	separately via the repo's `.github/secret_scanning.yml`. This replaced a former
66	repo-root `.gitleaksignore` whose `file:rule:line` fingerprints silently drifted.
67	
68	## Why these three levels
69	
70	The skill already surfaced three regressions during initial hand
71	verification — each one would have been caught here:
72	
73	| Regression                                                  | Caught by                |
74	|-------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
75	| Allowlist defaulted to `OR` between paths + regex           | `test_gitleaks_corpus`   |
76	| `[allowlist]` singular clashed with `[[allowlists]]` plural | `test_gitleaks_corpus`   |
77	| `gitleaks dir` silently skipped hidden paths                | `test_redact_secrets`    |
78	| JSON report `[]` treated as "leaks found"                   | `test_scan_staged.sh`    |
79	
80	## Requirements
81	
82	- `uv` (for `uv run --extra dev pytest`)
83	- `gitleaks` on `PATH` (corpus tests + shell test skip gracefully when
84	  missing — the pytest file xfails with a clear message, the shell
85	  test exits 0 for the "no gitleaks" case)
86	- `git` configured with a user identity (the shell test uses
87	  `-c user.email=...`)
88

```text
1	# Transcript & session discovery
2	
3	How `find-session.sh` locates "the session you are in right now" across
4	the fragmented landscape of coding-agent artifacts.
5	
6	## The core problem
7	
8	Several agents can be running in parallel against the same repository —
9	one Claude Code window, a background subagent, a Cursor window, plus
10	VS Code with the SpecStory extension auto-saving. Each writes into its
11	own directory using its own naming convention. There is no canonical
12	"current session" pointer; the best you can do is pick the freshest
13	artifact tied to `$PWD` and verify.
14	
15	## Claude Code session layout
16	
17	Claude Code stores each session as a JSON-lines file inside a
18	project-scoped directory:
19	
20	```
21	~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session-uuid>.jsonl
22	```
23	
24	The slug is the absolute working directory with **every non-alphanumeric
25	character** replaced by `-`, not just `/`. For
26	`$PWD=/Volumes/Data/Program/Personal/agent-skills` the slug is
27	`-Volumes-Data-Program-Personal-agent-skills` (leading dash included). A dot or
28	underscore collapses the same way, which is easy to miss:
29	`/home/<user>/.local/share/chezmoi` is stored as
30	`-home-<user>--local-share-chezmoi` — the dot becomes the second dash. Rebuild
31	the slug with `sed 's/[^A-Za-z0-9]/-/g'`, not `tr '/' '-'`, or a path
32	containing `.`/`_`/space silently resolves to a directory that doesn't exist
33	(`specstory sync` then reports `1 session not found`). The UUID is the Claude
34	session ID surfaced in `/status`.
35	
36	Heuristic: **the newest `.jsonl` in that directory is the active
37	session's transcript.** This breaks if you spawn a subagent that writes
38	into the same project dir and then stop interacting with the parent — the
39	subagent's JSONL wins by mtime. In practice the user knows which session
40	they're working in; the heuristic is fine for the "commit my chat" flow.
41	
42	## SpecStory history layout
43	
44	SpecStory writes one Markdown file per conversation:
45	
46	```
47	<repo-root>/.specstory/history/<timestamp>.md
48	```
49	
50	The timestamp is UTC ISO-8601-ish (e.g. `2026-04-24_05-05-10Z.md`). The
51	VS Code extension auto-saves continuously (controlled by
52	`specstory.autoSave`) so the file grows during the conversation. The CLI
53	(`specstory run claude`, `specstory sync claude -s <uuid>`) emits a new
54	file per session explicitly.
55	
56	Heuristic: **the newest `.md` in `.specstory/history/` is the active
57	transcript.** Same caveat as Claude — parallel sessions produce multiple
58	fresh files; mtime wins.
59	
60	## `find-session.sh` output shape
61	
62	TSV by default (two columns per line, tab-separated):
63	
64	```
65	specstory_path      <abs path or empty>
66	claude_session_uuid <uuid or empty>
67	claude_jsonl_path   <abs path or empty>
68	```
69	
70	`--json` emits a single-line JSON object. The script NEVER fails (always
71	exits 0) so agents can pipe it into downstream commands without
72	`set -e` explosions when a session isn't present.
73	
74	## When the heuristic breaks
75	
76	1. **Multiple concurrent agents in the same repo.** If you care which is
77	   "yours", open the session picker in your IDE (Claude Code's `/status`;
78	   SpecStory's session list) and grep for the UUID directly.
79	2. **Subagent writes a newer file than the parent.** After a long
80	   subagent run, the parent session's JSONL may look stale. The
81	   `--format=specstory` and `--format=claude` flags let you isolate one
82	   dimension.
83	3. **Repository renamed on disk.** Claude's slug is frozen at session
84	   start — if you `mv` the repo mid-session, the slug stops matching
85	   `$PWD`. Restart the agent to get a fresh session/slug pair.
86	4. **Worktrees.** `git worktree` directories have their own `$PWD` and
87	   thus their own slug. SpecStory stores per-worktree history too (it
88	   keys off `.specstory/history/` inside each worktree root).
89	
90	## SpecStory CLI integration (optional)
91	
92	If the user runs `specstory` directly:
93	
94	```bash
95	# Start a wrapped Claude Code session that auto-logs into .specstory/history/
96	specstory run claude
97	
98	# Sync a specific Claude session's JSONL into SpecStory's Markdown format
99	specstory sync claude -s <uuid>
100	
101	# List Claude sessions SpecStory knows about
102	specstory list claude
103	```
104	
105	When the VS Code extension is the source of truth (most common), the CLI
106	commands are unnecessary — the extension already wrote the file. Only
107	use `specstory sync` when you want to force-refresh a transcript for a
108	session whose files haven't auto-saved.
109	
110	## Cross-reference
111	
112	- [`pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](./pre-commit-redaction-stack.md) —
113	  how the located session files get scanned / redacted at commit time.
114	- [`../scripts/find-session.sh`](../scripts/find-session.sh) — the
115	  script implementing these heuristics.
116	- [`../scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh`](../scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh)
117	  — the caller that uses `find-session.sh --format=specstory` to locate
118	  the current transcript for `--session-only` staging.
119
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scan-staged.sh — run gitleaks on the current staged diff with
3	# agent-friendly exit codes.
4	#
5	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
6	
7	set -euo pipefail
8	
9	usage() {
10	  cat <<'EOF'
11	Usage: scan-staged.sh [OPTIONS]
12	
13	Scan the staged diff for secrets using `gitleaks git --staged`. Intended
14	as the "last line of defense" wrapper agents call before `git commit` so
15	they can branch on structured exit codes.
16	
17	Options:
18	  --redact           Pass --redact to gitleaks (default: off; findings
19	                     print the literal secret for debugging).
20	  --no-redact        Explicit opt-out of --redact (overrides --redact).
21	  --config PATH      Path to .gitleaks.toml (default: repo root if present).
22	  --verbose          Print gitleaks' own output to stderr.
23	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
24	
25	Output (stdout):
26	  - If clean: no output.
27	  - If leaks found: one JSON object per line with the finding details.
28	
29	Exit codes:
30	  0   clean — no secrets found
31	  10  leaks found (and redacted if --redact was passed)
32	  20  leaks found, not redacted (caller must rotate + re-stage)
33	  30  gitleaks binary not installed
34	  40  gitleaks error (bad config, unreadable repo, etc.)
35	  1   invalid arguments
36	  2   not inside a git repo
37	EOF
38	}
39	
40	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
41	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
42	
43	REDACT=0
44	CONFIG=""
45	VERBOSE=0
46	
47	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
48	  case "$1" in
49	    --redact)     REDACT=1; shift ;;
50	    --no-redact)  REDACT=0; shift ;;
51	    --config)     CONFIG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
52	    --config=*)   CONFIG="${1#--config=}"; shift ;;
53	    --verbose)    VERBOSE=1; shift ;;
54	    --help|-h)    usage; exit 0 ;;
55	    -*)           die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
56	    *)            die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
57	  esac
58	done
59	
60	# Check prerequisites.
61	if ! command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
62	  log "gitleaks not installed. Install hints:"
63	  log "  macOS:   brew install gitleaks"
64	  log "  Linux:   https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases"
65	  exit 30
66	fi
67	
68	if ! git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
69	  die "not inside a git repo" 2
70	fi
71	cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
72	
73	# Auto-discover config if not specified.
74	if [ -z "$CONFIG" ] && [ -f ".gitleaks.toml" ]; then
75	  CONFIG=".gitleaks.toml"
76	fi
77	
78	report_path="$(mktemp -t gitleaks-report.XXXXXX.json)"
79	trap 'rm -f "$report_path"' EXIT
80	
81	# Assemble the command. Post v8.19.0 `gitleaks git --staged` replaces the
82	# deprecated `gitleaks protect --staged`.
83	cmd=(gitleaks git --staged
84	     --report-format json
85	     --report-path "$report_path"
86	     --exit-code 0)
87	[ -n "$CONFIG" ] && cmd+=(--config "$CONFIG")
88	[ "$REDACT" = "1" ] && cmd+=(--redact)
89	
90	# Capture gitleaks' own exit code — with `--exit-code 0` it returns 0
91	# whether leaks are found or not, so a non-zero exit means the tool itself
92	# failed (config error, unreadable repo, etc.).
93	stderr_capture="$(mktemp -t gitleaks-stderr.XXXXXX)"
94	trap 'rm -f "$report_path" "$stderr_capture"' EXIT
95	
96	gl_rc=0
97	if [ "$VERBOSE" = "1" ]; then
98	  "${cmd[@]}" >&2 2>>"$stderr_capture" || gl_rc=$?
99	else
100	  "${cmd[@]}" >/dev/null 2>"$stderr_capture" || gl_rc=$?
101	fi
102	
103	if [ "$gl_rc" -ne 0 ]; then
104	  log "gitleaks failed to run (exit $gl_rc). Tail of its stderr:"
105	  tail -n 20 "$stderr_capture" >&2 || true
106	  exit 40
107	fi
108	
109	# Gitleaks writes an empty file when truly clean, or `[]` when the report
110	# format is JSON and there are zero findings. Normalize both to "clean".
111	if [ ! -s "$report_path" ]; then
112	  exit 0
113	fi
114	
115	finding_count=0
116	if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
117	  finding_count=$(python3 - "$report_path" <<'PY'
118	import json, sys
119	try:
120	    with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as f:
121	        data = json.load(f)
122	except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
123	    print(0)
124	    sys.exit(0)
125	print(len(data) if isinstance(data, list) else 0)
126	PY
127	)
128	else
129	  # Fallback: grep for a non-empty array. `[]` → 0, anything else → non-zero.
130	  case "$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$report_path")" in
131	    ""|"[]") finding_count=0 ;;
132	    *)        finding_count=1 ;;
133	  esac
134	fi
135	
136	if [ "$finding_count" -eq 0 ]; then
137	  exit 0
138	fi
139	
140	# Re-emit each finding as its own JSON object (one per line) for ergonomic
141	# agent consumption. Findings file is a JSON *array*; slice it into lines
142	# using python3 — avoid adding a jq dependency.
143	if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
144	  python3 - "$report_path" <<'PY'
145	import json, sys
146	with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as f:
147	    data = json.load(f)
148	for finding in data:
149	    # Keep only the most useful fields; caller can re-open the raw report.
150	    slim = {
151	        "rule_id": finding.get("RuleID"),
152	        "file": finding.get("File"),
153	        "line": finding.get("StartLine"),
154	        "commit": finding.get("Commit") or "STAGED",
155	        "match": finding.get("Match"),
156	    }
157	    print(json.dumps(slim, ensure_ascii=False))
158	PY
159	else
160	  # Fallback: dump the raw array.
161	  cat "$report_path"
162	fi
163	
164	if [ "$REDACT" = "1" ]; then
165	  log "gitleaks found leaks AND --redact was passed."
166	  log "  NOTE: gitleaks --redact only masks the CLI output, it does NOT"
167	  log "        rewrite files. Use redact_secrets.py --fix (or the pre-commit"
168	  log "        redact-agent-secrets hook) to actually scrub the artifacts."
169	  exit 10
170	else
171	  log "gitleaks found leaks. See JSON findings on stdout."
172	  log "Next: rotate the secret at the provider, then run redact_secrets.py --fix,"
173	  log "      then re-stage and re-run this check. DO NOT \`git push --force\`."
174	  exit 20
175	fi

2	# test_scan_staged.sh — exit-code contract for scripts/scan-staged.sh.
3	#
4	# Asserts the documented exit codes:
5	#   0   clean
6	#   20  leaks found
7	#   30  gitleaks binary missing
8	#    2  not inside a git repo
9	#
10	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
11	
12	set -u  # intentionally NOT -e: we capture non-zero exit codes
13	
14	TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
15	SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/.." && pwd)"
16	SCAN="$SKILL_DIR/scripts/scan-staged.sh"
17	FIXTURES="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures"
18	
19	# State (no associative arrays — bash 3.2 compat)
20	PASS_COUNT=0
21	FAIL_COUNT=0
22	FAIL_LOG=""
23	
24	red()   { printf '\033[31m%s\033[0m' "$*"; }
25	green() { printf '\033[32m%s\033[0m' "$*"; }
26	dim()   { printf '\033[2m%s\033[0m' "$*"; }
27	
28	pass() {
29	  PASS_COUNT=$((PASS_COUNT + 1))
30	  printf '  %s %s\n' "$(green PASS)" "$1"
31	}
32	fail() {
33	  FAIL_COUNT=$((FAIL_COUNT + 1))
34	  printf '  %s %s\n' "$(red FAIL)" "$1"
35	  FAIL_LOG="${FAIL_LOG}FAIL: $1\n"
36	}
37	
38	# make_repo — spin up an isolated tmp repo with an initial commit.
39	# Prints the path to stdout.
40	make_repo() {
41	  local d
42	  d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/test-scan-staged.XXXXXX)
43	  git -C "$d" init -q -b main
44	  git -C "$d" -c user.email=test@example.com -c user.name=test \
45	      commit -q --allow-empty -m init
46	  printf '%s' "$d"
47	}
48	
49	# Copy fixture + stage it under the given relative path. Strips the inline
50	# `<!-- gitleaks:allow -->` marker so the rules still fire in the throwaway repo
51	# (byte-identical to the fixture otherwise). Line-based sed → newline never
52	# enters the pattern space, so [[:space:]]* only eats the horizontal separator.
53	stage_fixture() {
54	  local repo="$1" fixture="$2" dest_rel="$3"
55	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$repo/$dest_rel")"
56	  sed 's/[[:space:]]*<!-- *gitleaks:allow *-->//g' "$FIXTURES/$fixture" > "$repo/$dest_rel"
57	  git -C "$repo" add -- "$dest_rel"
58	}
59	
60	if ! command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
61	  printf '%s gitleaks binary missing\n' "$(dim SKIP)"
62	  printf '  (skipping positive cases; running the exit-30 contract only)\n\n'
63	  GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE=0
64	else
65	  GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE=1
66	fi
67	
68	printf '== scan-staged exit-code contract ==\n\n'
69	
70	# --- Case 1: clean file → exit 0 ---
71	if [ "$GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE" = "1" ]; then
72	  REPO=$(make_repo)
73	  # Install the gitleaks config so rules apply.
74	  cp "$SKILL_DIR/assets/gitleaks.toml.template" "$REPO/.gitleaks.toml"
75	  stage_fixture "$REPO" "clean.md" "notes.md"
76	  (cd "$REPO" && bash "$SCAN" >/dev/null 2>&1)
77	  rc=$?
78	  if [ "$rc" = "0" ]; then pass "clean fixture → exit 0"
79	  else fail "clean fixture → exit 0 (got $rc)"
80	  fi
81	  rm -rf "$REPO"
82	fi
83	
84	# --- Case 2: real leak inside .claude/plans/ → exit 20 ---
85	if [ "$GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE" = "1" ]; then

87	  cp "$SKILL_DIR/assets/gitleaks.toml.template" "$REPO/.gitleaks.toml"

92	  else fail "real Anthropic key → exit 20 (got $rc)"
93	  fi
94	  rm -rf "$REPO"
95	fi
96	
97	# --- Case 3: not in a git repo → exit 2 ---
98	OUTSIDE=$(mktemp -d /tmp/test-scan-outside.XXXXXX)
99	(cd "$OUTSIDE" && bash "$SCAN" >/dev/null 2>&1)
100	rc=$?
101	if [ "$rc" = "2" ]; then pass "outside git repo → exit 2"
102	else fail "outside git repo → exit 2 (got $rc)"
103	fi
104	rm -rf "$OUTSIDE"
105	
106	# --- Case 4: gitleaks missing → exit 30 ---
107	# Simulate by running with an empty PATH so `command -v gitleaks` fails.
108	REPO=$(make_repo)
109	cp "$SKILL_DIR/assets/gitleaks.toml.template" "$REPO/.gitleaks.toml" 2>/dev/null || true
110	# Keep /bin and /usr/bin so the script itself (bash, git, mktemp) runs.
111	FAKE_PATH="/bin:/usr/bin"
112	(cd "$REPO" && PATH="$FAKE_PATH" bash "$SCAN" >/dev/null 2>&1)
113	rc=$?
114	if [ "$rc" = "30" ]; then pass "no gitleaks on PATH → exit 30"
115	else fail "no gitleaks on PATH → exit 30 (got $rc)"
116	fi
117	rm -rf "$REPO"
118	
119	# --- Case 5: empty JSON report `[]` handled as clean → exit 0 ---
120	# This is the regression we caught during initial verification: gitleaks
121	# writes `[]` for zero findings; scan-staged.sh must not treat that as
122	# "non-empty file → leaks found".
123	if [ "$GITLEAKS_AVAILABLE" = "1" ]; then
124	  REPO=$(make_repo)
125	  cp "$SKILL_DIR/assets/gitleaks.toml.template" "$REPO/.gitleaks.toml"

130	  else fail "allowlisted example shapes → exit 0 (got $rc)"
131	  fi
132	  rm -rf "$REPO"
133	fi
134	
135	printf '\n== summary ==\n'
136	printf 'pass: %d\nfail: %d\n' "$PASS_COUNT" "$FAIL_COUNT"
137	if [ "$FAIL_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
138	  printf '\n%b' "$FAIL_LOG"
139	  exit 1

1	"""Golden-corpus tests: stage each fixture in a throwaway git repo, run
2	`gitleaks git --staged` against `assets/gitleaks.toml.template`, and
3	assert the expected finding count.
4	
5	These catch regressions in:
6	- allowlist semantics (e.g. defaulting to OR instead of AND)
7	- config-file compatibility (e.g. mixing `[allowlist]` with `[[allowlists]]`)
8	- path-scoped allowlist paths drifting away from the real artifact dirs
9	
10	If gitleaks is not installed, the whole file skips.
11	"""
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import json
15	import re
16	import shutil
17	import subprocess
18	from pathlib import Path
19	
20	import pytest
21	
22	pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
23	    shutil.which("gitleaks") is None,
24	    reason="gitleaks binary not on PATH",

28	# Fixtures carry an inline `<!-- gitleaks:allow -->` marker so a repo-root or
29	# downstream gitleaks scan skips them by default. Strip it before staging and
30	# expand provider-scanner-sensitive placeholders so the secret bytes have the
31	# exact shape the rules expect and the assertions below still fire. No-op for
32	# lines without the marker
33	# (clean.md / example_shapes.md), which must keep their must-not-fire behavior.
34	_GITLEAKS_MARKER_RE = re.compile(r"[ \t]*<!--[ ]?gitleaks:allow[ ]?-->")
35	
36	
37	def _stage_fixture_at(repo: Path, fixture_path: Path, dest_rel: str) -> None:
38	    """Copy `fixture_path` to `repo/dest_rel`, stripping the inline
39	    `gitleaks:allow` marker, and git-add it."""
40	    dest = repo / dest_rel
41	    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
42	    text = fixture_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace(
43	        "__SYNTHETIC_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET__", "whsec_" + "a" * 32
44	    )
45	    dest.write_text(_GITLEAKS_MARKER_RE.sub("", text), encoding="utf-8")
46	    subprocess.run(["git", "add", "--", dest_rel], cwd=repo, check=True)
47	
48	
49	def _run_gitleaks_staged(repo: Path) -> list[dict]:
50	    """Run `gitleaks git --staged` and return the JSON findings array."""
51	    report = repo / "_report.json"
52	    result = subprocess.run(
53	        [
54	            "gitleaks",
55	            "git",
56	            "--staged",
57	            "--config",
58	            ".gitleaks.toml",
59	            "--report-format",
60	            "json",
61	            "--report-path",
62	            str(report),
63	            "--exit-code",
64	            "0",
65	        ],
66	        cwd=repo,
67	        capture_output=True,
68	        text=True,
69	    )
70	    # Non-zero would indicate config error — surface it for debugging.
71	    assert result.returncode == 0, (
72	        f"gitleaks failed:\nstdout: {result.stdout}\nstderr: {result.stderr}"
73	    )
74	    if not report.exists() or report.stat().st_size == 0:
75	        return []
76	    return json.loads(report.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

1	"""Regression tests for SpecStory's native secret redaction.
2	
3	SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts secrets when it writes a transcript. Two facts
4	about that behavior are load-bearing for this skill:
5	
6	1. It still redacts at all -- otherwise `.specstory/history/` is only as
7	   protected as our own pre-commit layer.
8	2. Its placeholder is still `[REDACTED:<label>]`. Our redactor writes the same
9	   shape and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, which is what makes the two
10	   layers idempotent instead of fighting each other over every commit.
11	
12	If upstream changes either one, this fails loudly rather than silently
13	re-introducing the redact -> re-stage -> re-commit loop.
14	
15	Skipped entirely when the specstory CLI is not installed.

1	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
2	# /// script
3	# requires-python = ">=3.11"

6	"""Measure which secret classes SpecStory's native redaction actually covers.
7	
8	SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts secrets from saved markdown (and cloud-synced
9	session data) by default, using the betterleaks ruleset. This probe answers
10	the only question that matters for our pre-commit layer: *what does it miss?*
11	
12	Method (no real agent session required):
13	
14	  1. Synthesize a Claude Code session JSONL under
15	     ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl for a throwaway project dir.
16	  2. Render it twice via `specstory sync claude -s <uuid> --print`:
17	     once with redaction on (default), once with --no-redact-secrets.
18	  3. Diff per token class -> covered / not covered, capturing the literal
19	     [REDACTED:<label>] placeholder SpecStory emitted.
20	  4. Re-scan the redacted markdown with our own .gitleaks.toml rules. Whatever
21	     still fires is the residual set our redactor must keep handling.
22	
23	Every probe token is generated at runtime from a seeded PRNG, so this file
24	contains key *shapes* but never a literal high-entropy token that would trip
25	a secret scanner on its own source.
26	
27	Usage:
28	    ./probe-specstory-redaction.py             # markdown table on stdout
29	    ./probe-specstory-redaction.py --json      # JSON lines on stdout
30	    ./probe-specstory-redaction.py --keep      # keep the synthetic session
31	    ./probe-specstory-redaction.py --dry-run   # print the plan, touch nothing
32	
33	Exit codes:
34	    0   probe completed
35	    2   `specstory sync` failed
36	   30   specstory CLI not on PATH

141	_SLUG_UNSAFE_RE = re.compile(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]")
142	
143	
144	def slug_for(path: Path) -> str:
145	    """Claude Code project slug for an absolute path.
146	
147	    Resolve symlinks first, then replace every non-alphanumeric character with
148	    '-', not just '/'. The realpath step is load-bearing on macOS, where
149	    `/var` resolves to `/private/var`: SpecStory derives the provider lookup
150	    from the physical subprocess cwd, so a slug built from the logical temp
151	    path produces "1 session not found".
152	
153	    Verified
154	    against a real session: `/home/<user>/.local/share/chezmoi` is stored as
155	    `-home-<user>--local-share-chezmoi` (the dot collapses to a second dash).
156	    Getting this wrong makes `specstory sync` report "1 session not found",
157	    which is why the probe also keeps its own temp path alphanumeric.
158	    """
159	    return _SLUG_UNSAFE_RE.sub("-", str(path.resolve()))

162	def build_session(project_dir: Path, catalog: list[dict]) -> tuple[Path, str]:
163	    """Write a synthetic Claude Code session JSONL. Returns (jsonl, session_id)."""
164	    session_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
165	    claude_dir = Path.home() / ".claude" / "projects" / slug_for(project_dir)

173	        "entrypoint": "cli",
174	        "cwd": str(project_dir),

183	    def add_user(text: str) -> None:

185	        node = str(uuid.uuid4())

199	        nonlocal parent

204	                "type": "assistant",

211	                    "stop_reason": "end_turn",
212	                    "usage": {"input_tokens": 1, "output_tokens": 1},
213	                },
214	                "uuid": node,
215	                "timestamp": now,
216	                **common,
217	            }
218	        )
219	        parent = node

221	    add_user("Probe session for agent-history-hygiene. Each turn carries one "
222	             "secret class in two contexts: an assignment and bare prose.")
223	    add_assistant("Understood, echoing each one back.")
224	
225	    for item in catalog:
226	        # Two distinct tokens per class: a shared token would let a single
227	        # replacement mask both contexts and fake a "covered" result.
228	        add_user(
229	            f"[class:{item['name']}:assign]\n"
230	            f"{item['name'].upper().replace('-', '_')}={item['token']}"
231	        )
232	        add_assistant(

234	            f"The tool printed {item['token_prose']} to stdout just now."
235	        )
236	
237	    add_user(

239	        + "\n".join(f"{name}: {value}" for name, value in NEGATIVE_CONTROLS)
240	    )
241	    add_assistant("Probe complete.")

243	    with jsonl.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
244	        for line in lines:

247	    return jsonl, session_id

250	def run_sync(project_dir: Path, session_id: str, redact: bool) -> str:
251	    cmd = [
252	        "specstory", "sync", "claude",
253	        "-s", session_id,
254	        "--print",
255	        "--no-cloud-sync",
256	        "--no-stats",
257	        "--no-usage-analytics",
258	        "--no-version-check",
259	        "--silent",
260	    ]
261	    if not redact:
262	        cmd.append("--no-redact-secrets")
263	    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=project_dir, capture_output=True, text=True)
264	    if proc.returncode != 0:
265	        detail = (proc.stderr or proc.stdout).strip()
266	        print(f"specstory sync failed (rc={proc.returncode}): {detail}",
267	              file=sys.stderr)
268	        if "session not found" in detail:
269	            print("hint: the synthetic session's Claude project slug did not "
270	                  "match. Check slug_for() against a real "
271	                  "~/.claude/projects/<slug> entry.", file=sys.stderr)
272	        raise SystemExit(2)
273	    return proc.stdout
274	
275	
276	_PLACEHOLDER_RE = re.compile(r"\[REDACTED:[^\]\s]+\]")
277	
278	
279	def classify(markdown: str, class_name: str, context: str, token: str) -> dict:
280	    """Determine whether `token` survived redaction in the given block."""
281	    marker = f"[class:{class_name}:{context}]"
282	    idx = markdown.find(marker)
283	    block = ""
284	    if idx >= 0:
285	        # The block runs until the next marker or the next section separator.
286	        rest = markdown[idx + len(marker):]
287	        stop = rest.find("[class:")
288	        block = rest if stop < 0 else rest[:stop]
289	
290	    present = token in block if block else token in markdown
291	    placeholders = _PLACEHOLDER_RE.findall(block)
292	    return {
293	        "present": present,
294	        "placeholders": sorted(set(placeholders)),
295	        "block_found": idx >= 0,
296	    }
297	
298	
299	def rule_for(token: str, findings: list[dict]) -> str | None:
300	    """Which of OUR gitleaks rules (if any) claims this token."""
301	    for finding in findings:
302	        secret = finding.get("Secret", "")
303	        if not secret:
304	            continue
305	        if secret in token or token in secret:
306	            return finding.get("RuleID", "?")
307	    return None
308	
309	
310	def gitleaks_scan(markdown: str) -> list[dict]:
311	    """Scan text with OUR gitleaks config; return findings."""
312	    if shutil.which("gitleaks") is None:
313	        return []
314	    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".json", delete=False) as f:
315	        report = f.name
316	    cmd = [
317	        "gitleaks", "stdin",
318	        "--report-format", "json",
319	        "--report-path", report,
320	        "--exit-code", "0",
321	    ]
322	    if GITLEAKS_CONFIG.is_file():
323	        cmd.extend(["--config", str(GITLEAKS_CONFIG)])
324	    try:
325	        subprocess.run(cmd, input=markdown, capture_output=True, text=True)
326	        content = Path(report).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
327	        return json.loads(content) if content.strip() else []
328	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, FileNotFoundError):
329	        return []
330	    finally:
331	        Path(report).unlink(missing_ok=True)
332	
333	
334	def specstory_version() -> str | None:
335	    if shutil.which("specstory") is None:
336	        return None
337	    proc = subprocess.run(["specstory", "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True)
338	    match = re.search(r"Current version:\s*([0-9][^\s│|]*)", proc.stdout)
339	    if match:
340	        return match.group(1).strip()
341	    match = re.search(r"([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)", proc.stdout)
342	    return match.group(1) if match else "unknown"
343	
344	
345	def redaction_config_state() -> str:
346	    """Report the effective [redaction] enabled setting we can see from config."""
347	    for candidate in (Path(".specstory/cli/config.toml"),
348	                      Path.home() / ".specstory/cli/config.toml"):
349	        if not candidate.is_file():
350	            continue
351	        text = candidate.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
352	        match = re.search(r"^\s*\[redaction\](.*?)(?=^\s*\[|\Z)", text,
353	                          re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL)
354	        if match and re.search(r"^\s*enabled\s*=\s*false", match.group(1), re.MULTILINE):
355	            return f"disabled by {candidate}"
356	        if match:
357	            return f"[redaction] block present in {candidate} (default on)"
358	    return "no [redaction] block in config -> default on"
359	
360	
361	def main() -> int:
362	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
363	        description="Probe which secret classes SpecStory's native redaction covers.",
364	        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
365	    )
366	    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true",
367	                        help="Emit JSON lines on stdout instead of a markdown table")
368	    parser.add_argument("--keep", action="store_true",
369	                        help="Keep the synthetic session + project dir for inspection")
370	    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
371	                        help="Describe what would run; create nothing")
372	    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20260818,
373	                        help="PRNG seed for synthetic tokens (default: 20260818)")
374	    args = parser.parse_args()
375	
376	    version = specstory_version()
377	    if version is None:
378	        print("specstory not found on PATH -- install it to run this probe.",
379	              file=sys.stderr)
380	        return 30
381	
382	    if args.dry_run:
383	        print(f"specstory {version}; redaction config: {redaction_config_state()}",
384	              file=sys.stderr)
385	        print("Would create a temp project dir, write a synthetic Claude Code "
386	              "session under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/, render it twice via "
387	              "`specstory sync claude --print` (with and without "
388	              "--no-redact-secrets), and diff per class.", file=sys.stderr)
389	        return 0

391	    rng = random.Random(args.seed)
392	    catalog = make_catalog(rng)
393	    # Second token per class for the prose context.
394	    prose_rng = random.Random(args.seed + 1)
395	    for item, prose_item in zip(catalog, make_catalog(prose_rng)):
396	        item["token_prose"] = prose_item["token"]
397	
398	    # Alphanumeric suffix on purpose: tempfile.mkdtemp() can emit '_', and a
399	    # slug-collapsed character makes the session undiscoverable (see slug_for).
400	    project_dir = (
401	        Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / f"specstoryprobe{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"
402	    ).resolve()
403	    project_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
404	    jsonl, session_id = build_session(project_dir, catalog)
405	    claude_dir = jsonl.parent
406	
407	    print(f"specstory {version}; redaction config: {redaction_config_state()}",
408	          file=sys.stderr)
409	    print(f"synthetic session: {jsonl}", file=sys.stderr)
410	
411	    try:
412	        redacted = run_sync(project_dir, session_id, redact=True)
413	        baseline = run_sync(project_dir, session_id, redact=False)
414	    finally:
415	        if not args.keep:
416	            shutil.rmtree(claude_dir, ignore_errors=True)
417	            shutil.rmtree(project_dir, ignore_errors=True)
418	        else:
419	            print(f"kept: {claude_dir} and {project_dir}", file=sys.stderr)
420	
421	    base_findings = gitleaks_scan(baseline)
422	    red_findings = gitleaks_scan(redacted)
423	
424	    rows: list[dict] = []
425	    for item in catalog:
426	        for context, token in (("assign", item["token"]),
427	                               ("prose", item["token_prose"])):
428	            base = classify(baseline, item["name"], context, token)
429	            red = classify(redacted, item["name"], context, token)
430	            covered = base["present"] and not red["present"]
431	            ours = rule_for(token, base_findings)
432	            if covered:
433	                verdict = "specstory"
434	            elif ours:
435	                verdict = "ours-residual"
436	            else:
437	                verdict = "uncovered"
438	            rows.append({
439	                "class": item["name"],
440	                "context": context,
441	                "in_baseline": base["present"],
442	                "in_redacted": red["present"],
443	                "covered": covered,
444	                "our_rule": ours,
445	                "verdict": verdict,
446	                "placeholders": red["placeholders"],
447	                "note": item.get("note", ""),
448	            })
449	
450	    for name, value in NEGATIVE_CONTROLS:
451	        rows.append({
452	            "class": f"negative:{name}",
453	            "context": "control",
454	            "in_baseline": value in baseline,
455	            "in_redacted": value in redacted,
456	            # For a negative control, "covered" means SpecStory wrongly redacted it.
457	            "covered": (value in baseline) and (value not in redacted),
458	            "our_rule": rule_for(value, base_findings),
459	            "verdict": "control",
460	            "placeholders": [],
461	            "note": "must survive redaction",
462	        })
463	
464	    residual_rules = sorted({f.get("RuleID", "?") for f in red_findings})
465	
466	    if args.json:
467	        for row in rows:
468	            print(json.dumps({"specstory": version, **row}, ensure_ascii=False))
469	        print(json.dumps({
470	            "specstory": version,
471	            "residual_gitleaks_rules": residual_rules,
472	            "residual_finding_count": len(red_findings),
473	        }, ensure_ascii=False))
474	    else:
475	        print(f"# SpecStory native redaction coverage (specstory {version})\n")
476	        print("| Class | Context | Caught by | Placeholder / our rule |")
477	        print("|---|---|---|---|")
478	        for row in rows:
479	            if not row["in_baseline"]:
480	                caught = "n/a (absent from baseline)"
481	                detail = "—"
482	            elif row["class"].startswith("negative:"):
483	                caught = "**redacted (false positive)**" if row["covered"] else "left alone"
484	                detail = f"`{row['our_rule']}`" if row["our_rule"] else "—"
485	            elif row["verdict"] == "specstory":
486	                caught = "SpecStory"
487	                detail = ", ".join(f"`{p}`" for p in row["placeholders"]) or "—"
488	            elif row["verdict"] == "ours-residual":
489	                caught = "**ours only**"
490	                detail = f"`{row['our_rule']}`"
491	            else:
492	                caught = "**nobody**"
493	                detail = "—"
494	            print(f"| `{row['class']}` | {row['context']} | {caught} | {detail} |")
495	        print()
496	        counts = {v: sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("verdict") == v)
497	                  for v in ("specstory", "ours-residual", "uncovered")}
498	        print(f"SpecStory: {counts['specstory']} · ours only: "
499	              f"{counts['ours-residual']} · uncovered by both: {counts['uncovered']}")
500	        print(f"\nResidual gitleaks findings against our config after SpecStory "
501	              f"redaction: {len(red_findings)}")
502	        if residual_rules:
503	            print("Rules still firing: " + ", ".join(f"`{r}`" for r in residual_rules))
504	
505	    missed = [r for r in rows
506	              if r["in_baseline"] and not r["covered"]
507	              and not r["class"].startswith("negative:")]
508	    print(f"\n{len(rows)} checks, {len(missed)} class/context pairs NOT covered "
