```text
1	# SpecStory's native redaction (v2.4.0+) and what it leaves us
2	
3	SpecStory redacts secrets on write, so this skill's pre-commit layer is no
4	longer the first line of defense for `.specstory/history/`. This page records
5	what upstream covers, what it misses, and why our layer still exists.
6	
7	Regenerate everything below with:
8	
9	```bash
10	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py
11	```
12	
13	## Upstream history
14	
15	| Ref | What |
16	|---|---|
17	| [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) | `feat(redaction): automatically redact secrets from saved markdown history` — community PR by [@warnes](https://github.com/warnes), merged 2026-07-20 |
18	| [PR #253](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/253) | A `gofmt` CI-fix fork of #235; closed in favor of #235 |
19	| **v2.4.0** (2026-07-20) | Shipped, **on by default**, covering local markdown **and** cloud sync |
20	| [#274](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/issues/274) (open) | Adjacent leak vector — `specstory watch` exposes the cloud auth token in its process command line |
21	
22	The merged implementation is not the one in the PR. The maintainer swapped the
23	PR's 11 inline regexes for the [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks)
24	library ("we can leverage that community that is thinking about secrets
25	redaction as their sole focus") and unified the code paths that needed
26	redaction.
27	
28	## Knobs
29	
30	```bash
31	specstory sync  --no-redact-secrets     # also on `run` and `watch`
32	```
33	
34	```toml
35	# .specstory/cli/config.toml (project) or ~/.specstory/cli/config.toml (user)
36	[redaction]
37	# Redact secrets and API keys from saved markdown history and cloud-synced
38	# session data. (default: true)
39	# enabled = false # equivalent to --no-redact-secrets
40	```
41	
42	**`enabled` is the only knob.** The PR's `extra_patterns` (custom regexes) did
43	not survive the Betterleaks rewrite — there are no `extra_patterns` or
44	`GetRedactionExtraPatterns` symbols in the 2.9.0 binary. Repo-specific rules
45	have no upstream equivalent and stay our layer's job.
46	
47	The placeholder is `[REDACTED:<betterleaks-rule-id>]` — the binary carries the
48	format string `[REDACTED:%s]`. Our redactor writes the same shape, and
49	`.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, so whichever layer runs first the other sees an
50	inert placeholder and leaves the file alone.
51	
52	## Coverage, measured
53	
54	Probed against **specstory 2.9.0** / gitleaks 8.30.0. Each class is tested in
55	two contexts with two distinct tokens: `assign` (`KEY=<token>`) and `prose`
56	(the token in a sentence, the way a tool transcript prints one).
57	
58	**SpecStory 36 · ours only 15 · uncovered by both 3** (of 54 class/context pairs)
59	
60	### The structural finding: prose is the blind spot
61	
62	Several classes are caught only in assignment context, and only by
63	betterleaks' entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule — which keys off a
64	`NAME = value` shape. The same token in prose sails through:
65	
66	| Class | `assign` | `prose` |
67	|---|---|---|
68	| `openai-project-key` | SpecStory (`generic-api-key`) | **ours** |
69	| `huggingface-token` | SpecStory (`generic-api-key`) | **ours** |
70	| `notion-integration-token` | SpecStory (`generic-api-key`) | **ours** |
71	| `wakatime-api-key` | SpecStory (`generic-api-key`) | **ours** |
72	| `stripe-webhook-secret` | SpecStory (`generic-api-key`) | **ours** |
73	
74	A transcript prints secrets in prose constantly — `cat .env` output, an error
75	message quoting a token, an agent echoing what it just read. Our
76	prefix-anchored rules do not care about surrounding syntax, so they hold in
77	both contexts.
78	
79	### Covered by SpecStory in both contexts
80	
81	`anthropic-api-key`, `openai-legacy-key`, `github-pat`,
82	`github-fine-grained-pat`, `github-oauth-token`, `github-actions-token`,
83	`gitlab-pat`, `google-api-key`, `groq-api-key`, `slack-bot-token`,
84	`stripe-secret-key`, `supabase-service-pat`, `linear-api-key`,
85	`private-key-pem`, `dotenv-dump`.
86	
87	Notable: `private-key-pem` → `[REDACTED:private-key]`, exactly the label our
88	redactor now writes for PEM blocks.
89	
90	### Ours in both contexts
91	
92	`cursor-api-key`, `tailscale-auth-key`, `discord-webhook-url`,
93	`zapier-webhook-url`, `make-webhook-url` — the custom rules in
94	`assets/gitleaks.toml.template`. Betterleaks does not ship rules for these.
95	
96	### Covered by nobody
97	
98	| Class | Why |
99	|---|---|
100	| `aws-access-key-id` (both contexts) | gitleaks 8.30.0 has no dedicated `AKIA…` rule any more, and betterleaks doesn't either. In assignment form a *generic* rule may catch it; bare in prose nothing does. An access key ID is only half a credential (the secret access key is the sensitive half, and that one is high-entropy enough to be caught), so this is a defensible upstream choice rather than a hole to patch. |
101	| `telegram-bot-token` (prose only) | Caught in assignment form, missed in prose. Add a custom rule if you paste bot tokens into transcripts. |
102	
103	### Negative controls
104	
105	`sk-proj-XXX...`, `sk-ant-api03-XXX...`, `your-api-key-here`, `example-key`
106	and `OPENAI_API_KEY=REDACTED` all survive both layers. Transcripts can still
107	discuss key shapes in prose.
108	
109	## What this means for our layer
110	
111	1. **Keep it.** 15 of 54 class/context pairs are ours alone, including every
112	   webhook URL rule and every prose-context custom key.
113	2. **Stop duplicating.** Our redactor writes SpecStory's placeholder shape and
114	   allowlists it, so a transcript SpecStory already cleaned is not rewritten —
115	   no "files were modified by this hook", no re-`git add`, no second commit.
116	3. **`--legacy` changes bytes, not detection.** It writes the pre-2.4.0
117	   placeholders (`sk-abc...xyz`, `[REDACTED PEM PRIVKEY BLOCK]`) for repos
118	   whose transcripts are full of the old sentinels and that would rather not
119	   mix the two shapes. Detection, scope, and exit codes are identical, so
120	   there is no reason to reach for it on a SpecStory older than 2.4.0 — our
121	   layer scans the same way regardless of what SpecStory did or didn't do.
122	4. **Below 2.4.0 our layer is the only layer.** Nothing changes in how it
123	   runs; there is simply no Layer 0 in front of it, so expect it to actually
124	   rewrite files instead of finding everything already clean.
125	
126	## Re-running the probe
127	
128	`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py` synthesizes a Claude Code session under
129	`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/`, renders it twice through
130	`specstory sync claude --print` (with and without `--no-redact-secrets`), diffs
131	per class, then re-scans the redacted markdown with our gitleaks config to
132	compute the residual set. It cleans up after itself unless `--keep`.
133	
134	The synthetic project path is resolved before deriving `<slug>`. On macOS,
135	`/var` resolves to `/private/var`; SpecStory looks up sessions from the physical
136	subprocess cwd, so using the unresolved temp path produces `1 session not
137	found`. See
138	[`pitfalls/specstory-sync-1-session-not-found-under-macos-var.md`](../../../../pitfalls/specstory-sync-1-session-not-found-under-macos-var.md).
139	
140	Probe tokens are generated at runtime from a seeded PRNG, so this repo carries
141	key *shapes* but never a literal high-entropy token that would trip a scanner
142	on the probe's own source.
143	
144	`tests/test_specstory_coverage.py` locks in the two facts we actually depend
145	on — that redaction is still on by default, and that the placeholder is still
146	`[REDACTED:<label>]` — and skips when `specstory` isn't installed.
147	
148	## Cross-reference
149	
150	- [`pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](./pre-commit-redaction-stack.md) — where
151	  this sits in the layered defense.
152	- [`../assets/redact_secrets.py`](../assets/redact_secrets.py) — the redactor
153	  and its `--legacy` flag.
154
```

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-28 07:26:37Z)**_

The redactor’s boundary is broader than the session selector problem but tightly coupled at commit time: it scans only configured artifact prefixes and Markdown, reads findings from the staged index, then rewrites the corresponding working-tree files; it does not itself re-stage despite `--fix` help saying “re-stage.” This staged-detection/working-tree-rewrite split is important for hook behavior and for any selector work, but selectors should likely reuse artifact classification without being added to secret filtering itself.

commit 5b78e2b61decd24a9ef2a024268526d4fdf0f99b
Author: Da-Wei Lee <daviddwlee84@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Aug 18 14:24:56 2026 +0800

    feat(agent-history-hygiene): align redaction with SpecStory native output
    
    SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts secrets on write (PR #235, shipped v2.4.0 via the
    Betterleaks ruleset, covering local markdown and cloud sync). Measure what it
    actually covers, then stop our pre-commit layer from redoing that work.
    
    Coverage, measured against specstory 2.9.0 over 54 class/context pairs:
    SpecStory 36, ours only 15, neither 3. The structural finding is that
    betterleaks catches several classes only in `KEY=value` form via its
    entropy-based generic-api-key rule -- the same token in prose, which is how a
    tool transcript actually prints one, sails through. Our prefix-anchored rules
    hold in both contexts, so this layer stays load-bearing.
    
    - redact_secrets.py writes `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`, the sentinel SpecStory
      emits natively (its binary carries the format string `[REDACTED:%s]`).
      PEM blocks become `[REDACTED:private-key]` -- SpecStory's own label for the
      class -- and stray headers `[REDACTED:private-key-header]`. Placeholders
      carry no secret bytes, so neither layer can re-flag the other's output and a
      second pass is a no-op. `--legacy` writes the pre-2.4.0 placeholders;
      it changes only the bytes written, never what is detected.
    - .gitleaks.toml allowlists the shared sentinel at regexTarget = "match", not
      "line": at line scope a line holding both a placeholder and a live key would
      be allowlisted wholesale.
    - detect-private-key honours neither `gitleaks:allow` markers nor
      .github/secret_scanning.yml -- it greps `BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY` as a plain
      substring -- so the pre-commit template excludes the skill's installed
      tests/ directory, which carries those headers on purpose.
    
    New probe + regression test:
    
    - scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py synthesizes a Claude Code session,
      renders it twice through `specstory sync --print` (with and without
      --no-redact-secrets), diffs per class, then re-scans the redacted markdown
      with our rules to compute the residual set. Probe tokens are generated at
      runtime from a seeded PRNG, so this repo carries key shapes but never a
      literal high-entropy token in the probe's own source.
    - tests/test_specstory_coverage.py locks in the two facts we depend on --
      redaction still on by default, placeholder still `[REDACTED:<label>]` --
      and skips when the CLI is absent.
    - references/specstory-native-redaction.md records the matrix, the upstream
      PRs, and the config knobs. Note `extra_patterns` did not survive the
      Betterleaks rewrite: `[redaction] enabled` is the only knob upstream, so
      repo-specific rules remain this layer's job.
    
    Two bugs found while building the probe:
    
    - Claude Code's project slug replaces EVERY non-alphanumeric character, not
      just `/`: `/home/<u>/.local/share/chezmoi` is stored as
      `-home-<u>--local-share-chezmoi`. find-session.sh used `sed 's|/|-|g'` and
      so returned nothing for any repo path containing `.`, `_` or a space.
      Fixed, and transcript-session-discovery.md corrected -- it asserted the
      wrong rule explicitly ("no other transformation").
    - The probe was flaky because tempfile.mkdtemp() can emit `_`, which the slug
      collapses; `specstory sync` then reports "1 session not found". Its temp
      path is now alphanumeric.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

new file mode 100755
index 0000000..a212152
--- /dev/null
+++ b/skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,117 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# find-session.sh — resolve the current agent session files for $PWD.
+#
+# Returns the SpecStory transcript path + Claude Code session UUID/JSONL
+# path for the current working directory, so the calling agent can stage
+# the right artifacts before a commit.
+#
+# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+usage() {
+  cat <<'EOF'
+Usage: find-session.sh [OPTIONS]
+
+Discover the agent session files associated with $PWD. Heuristics:
+  - SpecStory: newest *.md under ./.specstory/history/
+  - Claude Code: newest *.jsonl under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/ where
+                 <slug> is $PWD with '/' -> '-' (Claude's own convention).
+
+Options:
+  --format=VALUE     one of: specstory, claude, both (default: both)
+  --json             Emit JSON instead of TSV.
+  --quiet            Suppress stderr diagnostics on empty results.
+  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
+
+Output (TSV, one key/value per line):
+  specstory_path       <abs path or empty>
+  claude_session_uuid  <uuid or empty>
+  claude_jsonl_path    <abs path or empty>
+
+Exit codes:
+  0  always (never fails the pipeline; empty values signal absence).
+  1  invalid arguments.
+EOF
+}
+
+log()  { [ "$QUIET" = "1" ] || printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
+warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
+die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
+
+FORMAT="both"
+OUT_JSON=0
+QUIET=0
+
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --format=*) FORMAT="${1#--format=}"; shift ;;
+    --format)   FORMAT="${2:-both}"; shift 2 ;;
+    --json)     OUT_JSON=1; shift ;;
+    --quiet)    QUIET=1; shift ;;
+    --help|-h)  usage; exit 0 ;;
+    -*)         die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
+    *)          die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+case "$FORMAT" in
+  both|specstory|claude) ;;
+  *) die "invalid --format: $FORMAT (expected both|specstory|claude)" 1 ;;
+esac
+
+# Claude's project slug: absolute $PWD with '/' replaced by '-'.
+#   /Volumes/Data/x -> -Volumes-Data-x
+# The leading dash is intentional — it mirrors how Claude Code names the
+# subdirectory under ~/.claude/projects/.
+cwd_slug() {
+  printf '%s' "$PWD" | sed 's|/|-|g'
+}
+
+newest_file() {
+  # newest_file <dir> <glob>
+  # Prints the newest matching file by mtime, or empty if none.
+  local dir="$1" glob="$2"
+  [ -d "$dir" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
+  # stat -f on macOS, stat -c on Linux — use find+sort for portability.
+  local found
+  found=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$glob" -print0 2>/dev/null \
+    | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null \
+    | head -n 1)
+  printf '%s' "$found"
+}
+
+SPECSTORY_PATH=""
+CLAUDE_JSONL=""
+CLAUDE_UUID=""
+
+if [ "$FORMAT" = "both" ] || [ "$FORMAT" = "specstory" ]; then
+  candidate=$(newest_file "$PWD/.specstory/history" "*.md")
+  if [ -n "$candidate" ]; then
+    SPECSTORY_PATH="$candidate"
+  else
+    log "no .specstory/history/*.md under $PWD"
+  fi
+fi
+
+if [ "$FORMAT" = "both" ] || [ "$FORMAT" = "claude" ]; then
+  slug=$(cwd_slug)
+  proj_dir="$HOME/.claude/projects/$slug"
+  candidate=$(newest_file "$proj_dir" "*.jsonl")
+  if [ -n "$candidate" ]; then
+    CLAUDE_JSONL="$candidate"
+    CLAUDE_UUID=$(basename "$candidate" .jsonl)
+  else
+    log "no ~/.claude/projects/$slug/*.jsonl (slug derived from PWD)"
+  fi
+fi
+
+if [ "$OUT_JSON" = "1" ]; then
+  # Hand-rolled JSON keeps us dependency-free (no jq/python requirement).
+  printf '{"specstory_path":"%s","claude_session_uuid":"%s","claude_jsonl_path":"%s"}\n' \
+    "$SPECSTORY_PATH" "$CLAUDE_UUID" "$CLAUDE_JSONL"
+else
+  printf 'specstory_path\t%s\n' "$SPECSTORY_PATH"
+  printf 'claude_session_uuid\t%s\n' "$CLAUDE_UUID"
+  printf 'claude_jsonl_path\t%s\n' "$CLAUDE_JSONL"
+fi
```

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# stage-agent-artifacts.sh — git-add agent chat + plan artifacts before
+# the next commit.
+#
+# Default behavior: stage every dirty *.md under each directory in
+# assets/artifact-dirs.txt, plus the current SpecStory transcript.
+#
+# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
+SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
+DEFAULT_DIRS_FILE="$SKILL_DIR/assets/artifact-dirs.txt"
+
+usage() {
+  cat <<'EOF'
+Usage: stage-agent-artifacts.sh [OPTIONS]
+
+Stage agent artifact files (SpecStory transcripts, .claude/plans/*.md, etc.)
+for the next commit. Must be run from inside a git repo.
+
+Options:
+  --session-only        Only stage the current SpecStory transcript + newest
+                        plan file; skip .cursor/, .opencode/, etc.
+  --include-all-plans   Also re-add already-tracked plan/transcript files
+                        that were modified (default: only unstaged files).
+  --dirs-file PATH      Override the default artifact-dirs.txt location.
+  --dry-run             Print the files that would be staged, but don't stage.
+  --allow-empty         Stage artifacts even when HEAD has no code changes
+                        (default: refuse — prevents "commit just transcript").
+  --help, -h            Show this help and exit.
+
+Exit codes:
+  0  success (one or more artifacts staged or already clean)
+  1  invalid arguments
+  2  not inside a git repo
+  3  no code changes AND no dirty artifacts (suggests nothing to commit)
+  4  refused: code is clean but artifacts are dirty (use --allow-empty)
+EOF
+}
+
+log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
+warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
+die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
+
+SESSION_ONLY=0
+INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS=0
+DIRS_FILE="$DEFAULT_DIRS_FILE"
+DRY_RUN=0
+ALLOW_EMPTY=0
+
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --session-only)       SESSION_ONLY=1; shift ;;
+    --include-all-plans)  INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS=1; shift ;;
+    --dirs-file)          DIRS_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
+    --dirs-file=*)        DIRS_FILE="${1#--dirs-file=}"; shift ;;
+    --dry-run)            DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
+    --allow-empty)        ALLOW_EMPTY=1; shift ;;
+    --help|-h)            usage; exit 0 ;;
+    -*)                   die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
+    *)                    die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+# Must be in a git repo.
+if ! git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  die "not inside a git repo" 2
+fi
+REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
+cd "$REPO_ROOT"
+
+# Read artifact dirs from the config file.
+if [ ! -f "$DIRS_FILE" ]; then
+  die "artifact-dirs.txt not found: $DIRS_FILE" 1
+fi
+
+ARTIFACT_DIRS=()
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  # Strip comments and whitespace.
+  line="${line%%#*}"
+  line="$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')"
+  [ -n "$line" ] && ARTIFACT_DIRS+=("$line")
+done < "$DIRS_FILE"
+
+# Warn if any artifact dir is silently gitignored.
+check_ignored() {
+  local dir="$1"
+  # `git check-ignore` exits 0 if the path matches an ignore rule.
+  if [ -e "$dir" ] && git check-ignore -q "$dir" 2>/dev/null; then
+    warn "$dir is gitignored — staged files under it won't actually be committed"
+  fi
+}
+
+# Resolve the "current session" artifacts for --session-only.
+find_current_specstory() {
+  "$SCRIPT_DIR/find-session.sh" --quiet --format=specstory 2>/dev/null \
+    | awk -F'\t' '$1=="specstory_path"{print $2}'
+}
+find_current_plan() {
+  [ -d ".claude/plans" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
+  find .claude/plans -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.md' -print0 2>/dev/null \
+    | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null | head -n 1
+}
+
+# List dirty artifact files across the configured dirs.
+# Returns null-separated paths on stdout.
+list_dirty_artifacts() {
+  local dir path git_status
+  for dir in "${ARTIFACT_DIRS[@]}"; do
+    [ -e "$dir" ] || continue
+    check_ignored "$dir"
+    # Include untracked (??) and modified (M/A) entries. `-z` → NUL separated.
+    while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
+      # porcelain -z format: XY<space>path[\0orig_path]
+      # We only want the path portion.
+      git_status="${entry:0:2}"
+      path="${entry:3}"
+      case "$path" in
+        *.md) ;;
+        *) continue ;;
+      esac
+      case "$git_status" in
+        "??") printf '%s\0' "$path" ;;
+        " M"|"MM"|"AM"|"AD"|"A ") printf '%s\0' "$path" ;;
+        "M "|"A ")
+          # Already staged — only re-add if --include-all-plans.
+          [ "$INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS" = "1" ] && printf '%s\0' "$path"
+          ;;
+      esac
+    done < <(git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall -- "$dir" 2>/dev/null || true)
+  done
+}
+
+# --- Main ---
+STAGED_COUNT=0
+CANDIDATES=()
+
+if [ "$SESSION_ONLY" = "1" ]; then
+  specstory=$(find_current_specstory)
+  plan=$(find_current_plan)
+  [ -n "$specstory" ] && [ -f "$specstory" ] && CANDIDATES+=("$specstory")
+  [ -n "$plan" ] && [ -f "$plan" ] && CANDIDATES+=("$plan")
+else
+  # Capture the dirty artifact list.
+  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
+    CANDIDATES+=("$f")
+  done < <(list_dirty_artifacts)
+fi
+
+# Check: are there code changes outside the artifact dirs?
+# Non-artifact dirty files (staged or unstaged) mean the agent is committing
+# a real feature alongside the transcript — that's the intended use.
+has_code_changes() {
+  local any=0 line path in_artifact dir
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -z "$line" ] && continue
+    path="${line:3}"
+    in_artifact=0
+    for dir in "${ARTIFACT_DIRS[@]}"; do
+      case "$path" in
+        "$dir"/*) in_artifact=1; break ;;
+      esac
+    done
+    [ "$in_artifact" = "0" ] && any=1
+  done < <(git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain=v1 2>/dev/null)
+  [ "$any" = "1" ]
+}
+
+if [ "${#CANDIDATES[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
+  if has_code_changes; then
+    log "No agent artifacts to stage; code changes present — nothing to do."
+    exit 0
+  fi
+  log "Nothing to stage: no code changes and no dirty artifacts."
+  exit 3
+fi
+
+if [ "$ALLOW_EMPTY" = "0" ] && ! has_code_changes; then
+  log "Refusing: artifacts are dirty but no code changes staged."
+  log "         A transcript/plan commit without a feature diff is usually wrong."
+  log "         Re-run with --allow-empty if you really want to commit artifacts alone."
+  exit 4
+fi
+
+# Stage (or print).
+for f in "${CANDIDATES[@]}"; do
+  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
+    printf '[dry-run] would git add: %s\n' "$f"
+  else
+    git add -- "$f"
+    printf 'staged: %s\n' "$f"
+  fi
+  STAGED_COUNT=$((STAGED_COUNT + 1))
+done
+
+log "${STAGED_COUNT} artifact(s) ${DRY_RUN:+would be }staged."
```

1	# Plan: `agent-history-hygiene` skill
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	The user tracks agent chat history with **SpecStory** (`.specstory/history/*.md`) and keeps Claude Code plan files in-repo via `plansDirectory: "./.claude/plans"`, committing both alongside the feature diff that produced them. The workflow already works for the user locally — chezmoi carries a `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook, a comprehensive `.gitleaks.toml`, and a global `core.hooksPath` wrapper.
6	
7	Three gaps remain:
8	
9	1. **Default LLM behavior drifts against the user's intent.** Agents treat `.specstory/history/*.md` and `.claude/plans/*.md` as auto-generated artifacts and exclude them from commits unless told otherwise. There's no skill capturing the "always commit these, and find *your* session among many" rule.
10	2. **The infrastructure doesn't transplant cleanly.** A fresh repo without chezmoi has no pre-commit config, no gitleaks rules, and no `plansDirectory` — the user wants a single `bootstrap-project.sh` instead of per-repo drudgery.
11	3. **Post-leak discipline isn't captured.** When secrets slip into a transcript the user wants the skill to enforce rotate-first, rewrite-last — explicitly steering agents away from reflexive `git push --force` to "scrub" a shared branch.
12	
13	This plan creates `skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/` as the canonical surface. Chezmoi changes are intentionally minimal — the existing stack is 90% there; the skill adds the glue and the agent-facing discipline.
14	
15	## Recommended approach
16	
17	Create a single local skill with 4 scripts, 3 reference docs, and 4 assets. Make one small chezmoi addition (SpecStory/plans allowlist) and one small chezmoi fix (deprecated `gitleaks protect` → `gitleaks git --staged`).
18	
19	### Decisions locked in (from user answers)
20	
21	- **Name**: `agent-history-hygiene`
22	- **Artifact scope**: `.specstory/history/`, `.claude/plans/`, `.cursor/plans/`, `.cursor/rules/`, `.opencode/plans/`, `.specify/`, `.codex/` — plus a configurable list (`assets/artifact-dirs.txt`) so new agent dirs get picked up without editing scripts.
23	- **Auto-stage**: ship `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` agent-invoked by default; provide `bootstrap-project.sh --install-hook` for optional git `prepare-commit-msg` auto-stage.
24	- **Redactor**: bundle `redact_secrets.py` under `assets/`. Document the chezmoi version as upstream-of-record; sync procedure spelled out in `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.

47	### 2. `SKILL.md` outline
48	
49	Frontmatter `description` — pushy, trigger-dense, ~55 words. Mentions: "commit my chat", "save specstory session", "stage the plan file", "scrub transcript", "my .env leaked in chat", "bootstrap pre-commit", plus the passive trigger "you see untracked `.specstory/history/` during `git status`".

53	1. **Core invariants** — three rules: commit transcripts + plans alongside diff; rotate-at-provider *before* any git rewrite; never `--force` against a shared branch to hide a leak.

55	3. **Integration with existing infrastructure** — points at chezmoi's `redact-agent-secrets` + `.gitleaks.toml` + global `core.hooksPath`; explains what this skill adds (invocation + bootstrap + agent-facing discipline) vs what chezmoi owns (rules + redactor source-of-truth).

57	5. **Workflow B: bootstrap a new project** — `bootstrap-project.sh` (optionally `--install-hook`, `--from-chezmoi`) → audit `.gitignore` won't silently hide artifacts.

67	**`find-session.sh [--json] [--format=specstory|claude|both]`**
68	- Claude UUID = newest `*.jsonl` in `~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/` (slug = `$PWD` with `/` → `-`).
69	- SpecStory path = newest `*.md` in `$PWD/.specstory/history/`.

72	**`stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--dry-run] [--include-all-plans] [--session-only] [--dirs-file PATH]`**

75	- `--session-only`: just the current SpecStory file + current plan file.
76	- Refuses to run if HEAD has no code changes + no dirty artifacts (prevents the "commit just the transcript" anti-pattern).
77

83	  4. `uvx pre-commit@4 install` (pinned, hermetic).
84	  5. `--install-hook` only: also write a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only` so every commit auto-attaches the current session.
85	  6. Audit `.gitignore` and `.git/info/exclude` — warn (don't edit) if any configured artifact dir matches an ignore pattern.
86	  7. Verify `~/.claude/settings.json` has `plansDirectory: "./.claude/plans"`; if not, print the exact JSON patch (don't silently edit).
87	
88	**`scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--no-redact] [--verbose]`**
89	- Uses `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (current syntax, not deprecated `protect`).
90	- Exit codes: `0` = clean, `10` = leaks + redacted, `20` = leaks + no-redact, `30` = gitleaks missing (prints install hint).
91	- JSON-lines findings to stdout; prose to stderr.

1	"""Regression tests for SpecStory's native secret redaction.
2	
3	SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts secrets when it writes a transcript. Two facts
4	about that behavior are load-bearing for this skill:
5	
6	1. It still redacts at all -- otherwise `.specstory/history/` is only as
7	   protected as our own pre-commit layer.
8	2. Its placeholder is still `[REDACTED:<label>]`. Our redactor writes the same
9	   shape and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, which is what makes the two
10	   layers idempotent instead of fighting each other over every commit.
11	
12	If upstream changes either one, this fails loudly rather than silently
13	re-introducing the redact -> re-stage -> re-commit loop.
14	
15	Skipped entirely when the specstory CLI is not installed.
16	"""

45	    if proc.returncode == 30:

48	    rows = [json.loads(line) for line in proc.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]
49	    assert rows, "probe produced no rows"
50	    return rows

6	import subprocess
7	from pathlib import Path
8	
9	
10	SKILL_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
11	BOOTSTRAP = SKILL_DIR / "scripts" / "bootstrap-project.sh"
12	
13	
14	def git(repo: Path, *args: str, check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
15	    return subprocess.run(
16	        ["git", *args],
17	        cwd=repo,
18	        check=check,
19	        capture_output=True,
20	        text=True,
21	    )
22	
23	
24	def init_repo(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
25	    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
26	    repo.mkdir()
27	    git(repo, "init", "-q")
28	    git(repo, "config", "user.email", "agent-history-test@example.invalid")
29	    git(repo, "config", "user.name", "Agent History Test")
30	    # Avoid installing real hooks in the throwaway repo. bootstrap treats an
31	    # existing custom hooksPath as an intentional global-wrapper setup.
32	    git(repo, "config", "core.hooksPath", ".test-hooks")
33	    return repo
34	
35	
36	def run_bootstrap(repo: Path, tmp_path: Path, *args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
37	    env = os.environ.copy()
38	    env["HOME"] = str(tmp_path / "home")
39	    return subprocess.run(
40	        ["bash", str(BOOTSTRAP), *args],
41	        cwd=repo,
42	        env=env,
43	        check=True,
44	        capture_output=True,
45	        text=True,
46	    )
47	
48	
49	def test_adds_precise_rules_idempotently_and_keeps_history_visible(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
50	    repo = init_repo(tmp_path)
51	
52	    run_bootstrap(repo, tmp_path)
53	    ignore_file = repo / ".specstory" / ".gitignore"
54	    first = ignore_file.read_text()
55	    run_bootstrap(repo, tmp_path)
56	
57	    assert ignore_file.read_text() == first
58	    assert first.count("/.project.json") == 1
59	    assert first.count("/statistics.json") == 1
60	
61	    history = repo / ".specstory" / "history" / "session.md"
62	    history.parent.mkdir()
63	    history.write_text("# Session\n")
64	    ignored = git(repo, "check-ignore", "-q", str(history.relative_to(repo)), check=False)
65	    assert ignored.returncode == 1
66	
67	
68	def test_preserves_existing_nested_ignore_content(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
69	    repo = init_repo(tmp_path)
70	    ignore_file = repo / ".specstory" / ".gitignore"
71	    ignore_file.parent.mkdir()
72	    ignore_file.write_text("# keep me\n/custom-local.json")
73	
74	    run_bootstrap(repo, tmp_path)
75	    content = ignore_file.read_text()
76	
77	    assert content.startswith("# keep me\n/custom-local.json\n")
78	    assert content.count("/.project.json") == 1
79	    assert content.count("/statistics.json") == 1
80	
81	
82	def test_dry_run_does_not_create_specstory_directory(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
83	    repo = init_repo(tmp_path)
84	
85	    result = run_bootstrap(repo, tmp_path, "--dry-run")
86	
87	    assert not (repo / ".specstory").exists()
88	    assert "[dry-run] add '/.project.json'" in result.stderr
89	    assert "[dry-run] add '/statistics.json'" in result.stderr
90	
91	
92	def test_tracked_state_warns_until_explicitly_untracked(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
93	    repo = init_repo(tmp_path)
94	    specstory = repo / ".specstory"
95	    specstory.mkdir()
96	    project = specstory / ".project.json"
97	    statistics = specstory / "statistics.json"
98	    project.write_text('{"workspace_id":"machine-a"}\n')
99	    statistics.write_text('{"sessions":{}}\n')
100	    git(repo, "add", "-f", ".specstory/.project.json", ".specstory/statistics.json")
101	    git(repo, "commit", "-qm", "track old SpecStory state")
102	    statistics.write_text('{"sessions":{"new-machine":{}}}\n')
103	
104	    warned = run_bootstrap(repo, tmp_path)
105	    assert "SpecStory machine state is already tracked" in warned.stderr
106	    assert git(repo, "ls-files", ".specstory/.project.json").stdout.strip()
107	    assert git(repo, "ls-files", ".specstory/statistics.json").stdout.strip()
108	
109	    migrated = run_bootstrap(repo, tmp_path, "--untrack-specstory-state")
110	    assert "files remain on disk" in migrated.stderr
111	    assert project.exists()
112	    assert statistics.exists()
113	    assert git(repo, "ls-files", ".specstory/.project.json").stdout == ""
114	    assert git(repo, "ls-files", ".specstory/statistics.json").stdout == ""
115	    assert "D  .specstory/.project.json" in git(repo, "status", "--short").stdout
116	    assert "D  .specstory/statistics.json" in git(repo, "status", "--short").stdout

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# find-session.sh — resolve the current agent session files for $PWD.
3	#
4	# Returns the SpecStory transcript path + Claude Code session UUID/JSONL
5	# path for the current working directory, so the calling agent can stage
6	# the right artifacts before a commit.
7	#
8	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
9	
10	set -euo pipefail
11	
12	usage() {
13	  cat <<'EOF'
14	Usage: find-session.sh [OPTIONS]
15	
16	Discover the agent session files associated with $PWD. Heuristics:
17	  - SpecStory: newest *.md under ./.specstory/history/
18	  - Claude Code: newest *.jsonl under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/ where
19	                 <slug> is $PWD with '/' -> '-' (Claude's own convention).
20	
21	Options:
22	  --format=VALUE     one of: specstory, claude, both (default: both)
23	  --json             Emit JSON instead of TSV.
24	  --quiet            Suppress stderr diagnostics on empty results.
25	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
26	
27	Output (TSV, one key/value per line):
28	  specstory_path       <abs path or empty>
29	  claude_session_uuid  <uuid or empty>
30	  claude_jsonl_path    <abs path or empty>
31	
32	Exit codes:
33	  0  always (never fails the pipeline; empty values signal absence).
34	  1  invalid arguments.
35	EOF
36	}
37	
38	log()  { [ "$QUIET" = "1" ] || printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
39	warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
40	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
41	
42	FORMAT="both"
43	OUT_JSON=0
44	QUIET=0
45	
46	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
47	  case "$1" in
48	    --format=*) FORMAT="${1#--format=}"; shift ;;
49	    --format)   FORMAT="${2:-both}"; shift 2 ;;
50	    --json)     OUT_JSON=1; shift ;;
51	    --quiet)    QUIET=1; shift ;;
52	    --help|-h)  usage; exit 0 ;;
53	    -*)         die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
54	    *)          die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
55	  esac
56	done
57	
58	case "$FORMAT" in
59	  both|specstory|claude) ;;
60	  *) die "invalid --format: $FORMAT (expected both|specstory|claude)" 1 ;;
61	esac
62	
63	# Claude's project slug: absolute $PWD with every NON-ALPHANUMERIC character
64	# replaced by '-' -- not just '/'.
65	#   /Volumes/Data/x          -> -Volumes-Data-x
66	#   /home/u/.local/share/foo -> -home-u--local-share-foo   (the dot collapses)
67	# The leading dash is intentional -- it mirrors how Claude Code names the
68	# subdirectory under ~/.claude/projects/. Using `tr '/' '-'` here silently
69	# returns an empty result for any path containing '.', '_' or a space.
70	cwd_slug() {
71	  printf '%s' "$PWD" | sed 's|[^A-Za-z0-9]|-|g'
72	}
73	
74	newest_file() {
75	  # newest_file <dir> <glob>
76	  # Prints the newest matching file by mtime, or empty if none.
77	  local dir="$1" glob="$2"
78	  [ -d "$dir" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
79	  # stat -f on macOS, stat -c on Linux — use find+sort for portability.
80	  local found
81	  found=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "$glob" -print0 2>/dev/null \
82	    | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null \
83	    | head -n 1)
84	  printf '%s' "$found"
85	}
86	
87	SPECSTORY_PATH=""
88	CLAUDE_JSONL=""
89	CLAUDE_UUID=""
90	
91	if [ "$FORMAT" = "both" ] || [ "$FORMAT" = "specstory" ]; then
92	  candidate=$(newest_file "$PWD/.specstory/history" "*.md")
93	  if [ -n "$candidate" ]; then
94	    SPECSTORY_PATH="$candidate"
95	  else
96	    log "no .specstory/history/*.md under $PWD"
97	  fi
98	fi
99	
100	if [ "$FORMAT" = "both" ] || [ "$FORMAT" = "claude" ]; then
101	  slug=$(cwd_slug)
102	  proj_dir="$HOME/.claude/projects/$slug"
103	  candidate=$(newest_file "$proj_dir" "*.jsonl")
104	  if [ -n "$candidate" ]; then
105	    CLAUDE_JSONL="$candidate"
106	    CLAUDE_UUID=$(basename "$candidate" .jsonl)
107	  else
108	    log "no ~/.claude/projects/$slug/*.jsonl (slug derived from PWD)"
109	  fi
110	fi
111	
112	if [ "$OUT_JSON" = "1" ]; then
113	  # Hand-rolled JSON keeps us dependency-free (no jq/python requirement).
114	  printf '{"specstory_path":"%s","claude_session_uuid":"%s","claude_jsonl_path":"%s"}\n' \
115	    "$SPECSTORY_PATH" "$CLAUDE_UUID" "$CLAUDE_JSONL"
116	else
117	  printf 'specstory_path\t%s\n' "$SPECSTORY_PATH"
118	  printf 'claude_session_uuid\t%s\n' "$CLAUDE_UUID"
119	  printf 'claude_jsonl_path\t%s\n' "$CLAUDE_JSONL"
120	fi
121

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# stage-agent-artifacts.sh — git-add agent chat + plan artifacts before
3	# the next commit.
4	#
5	# Default behavior: stage every dirty *.md under each directory in
6	# assets/artifact-dirs.txt, plus the current SpecStory transcript.
7	#
8	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
9	
10	set -euo pipefail
11	
12	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
13	SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
14	DEFAULT_DIRS_FILE="$SKILL_DIR/assets/artifact-dirs.txt"
15	
16	usage() {
17	  cat <<'EOF'
18	Usage: stage-agent-artifacts.sh [OPTIONS]
19	
20	Stage agent artifact files (SpecStory transcripts, .claude/plans/*.md, etc.)
21	for the next commit. Must be run from inside a git repo.
22	
23	Options:
24	  --session-only        Only stage the current SpecStory transcript + newest
25	                        plan file; skip .cursor/, .opencode/, etc.
26	  --include-all-plans   Also re-add already-tracked plan/transcript files
27	                        that were modified (default: only unstaged files).
28	  --dirs-file PATH      Override the default artifact-dirs.txt location.
29	  --dry-run             Print the files that would be staged, but don't stage.
30	  --allow-empty         Stage artifacts even when HEAD has no code changes
31	                        (default: refuse — prevents "commit just transcript").
32	  --help, -h            Show this help and exit.
33	
34	Exit codes:
35	  0  success (one or more artifacts staged or already clean)
36	  1  invalid arguments
37	  2  not inside a git repo
38	  3  no code changes AND no dirty artifacts (suggests nothing to commit)
39	  4  refused: code is clean but artifacts are dirty (use --allow-empty)
40	EOF
41	}
42	
43	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
44	warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
45	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
46	
47	SESSION_ONLY=0
48	INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS=0
49	DIRS_FILE="$DEFAULT_DIRS_FILE"
50	DRY_RUN=0
51	ALLOW_EMPTY=0
52	
53	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
54	  case "$1" in
55	    --session-only)       SESSION_ONLY=1; shift ;;
56	    --include-all-plans)  INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS=1; shift ;;
57	    --dirs-file)          DIRS_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
58	    --dirs-file=*)        DIRS_FILE="${1#--dirs-file=}"; shift ;;
59	    --dry-run)            DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
60	    --allow-empty)        ALLOW_EMPTY=1; shift ;;
61	    --help|-h)            usage; exit 0 ;;
62	    -*)                   die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
63	    *)                    die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
64	  esac
65	done
66	
67	# Must be in a git repo.
68	if ! git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
69	  die "not inside a git repo" 2
70	fi
71	REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
72	cd "$REPO_ROOT"
73	
74	# Read artifact dirs from the config file.
75	if [ ! -f "$DIRS_FILE" ]; then
76	  die "artifact-dirs.txt not found: $DIRS_FILE" 1
77	fi
78	
79	ARTIFACT_DIRS=()
80	while IFS= read -r line; do
81	  # Strip comments and whitespace.
82	  line="${line%%#*}"
83	  line="$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')"
84	  [ -n "$line" ] && ARTIFACT_DIRS+=("$line")
85	done < "$DIRS_FILE"
86	
87	# Warn if any artifact dir is silently gitignored.
88	check_ignored() {
89	  local dir="$1"
90	  # `git check-ignore` exits 0 if the path matches an ignore rule.
91	  if [ -e "$dir" ] && git check-ignore -q "$dir" 2>/dev/null; then
92	    warn "$dir is gitignored — staged files under it won't actually be committed"
93	  fi
94	}
95	
96	# Resolve the "current session" artifacts for --session-only.
97	find_current_specstory() {
98	  "$SCRIPT_DIR/find-session.sh" --quiet --format=specstory 2>/dev/null \
99	    | awk -F'\t' '$1=="specstory_path"{print $2}'
100	}
101	find_current_plan() {
102	  [ -d ".claude/plans" ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
103	  find .claude/plans -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.md' -print0 2>/dev/null \
104	    | xargs -0 ls -t 2>/dev/null | head -n 1
105	}
106	
107	# List dirty artifact files across the configured dirs.
108	# Returns null-separated paths on stdout.
109	list_dirty_artifacts() {
110	  local dir path git_status
111	  for dir in "${ARTIFACT_DIRS[@]}"; do
112	    [ -e "$dir" ] || continue
113	    check_ignored "$dir"
114	    # Include untracked (??) and modified (M/A) entries. `-z` → NUL separated.
115	    while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
116	      # porcelain -z format: XY<space>path[\0orig_path]
117	      # We only want the path portion.
118	      git_status="${entry:0:2}"
119	      path="${entry:3}"
120	      case "$path" in
121	        *.md) ;;
122	        *) continue ;;
123	      esac
124	      case "$git_status" in
125	        "??") printf '%s\0' "$path" ;;
126	        " M"|"MM"|"AM"|"AD"|"A ") printf '%s\0' "$path" ;;
127	        "M "|"A ")
128	          # Already staged — only re-add if --include-all-plans.
129	          [ "$INCLUDE_ALL_PLANS" = "1" ] && printf '%s\0' "$path"
130	          ;;
131	      esac
132	    done < <(git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall -- "$dir" 2>/dev/null || true)
133	  done
134	}
135	
136	# --- Main ---
137	STAGED_COUNT=0
138	CANDIDATES=()
139	
140	if [ "$SESSION_ONLY" = "1" ]; then
141	  specstory=$(find_current_specstory)
142	  plan=$(find_current_plan)
143	  [ -n "$specstory" ] && [ -f "$specstory" ] && CANDIDATES+=("$specstory")
144	  [ -n "$plan" ] && [ -f "$plan" ] && CANDIDATES+=("$plan")
145	else

147	  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
148	    CANDIDATES+=("$f")
149	  done < <(list_dirty_artifacts)
150	fi

152	# Check: are there code changes outside the artifact dirs?
153	# Non-artifact dirty files (staged or unstaged) mean the agent is committing
154	# a real feature alongside the transcript — that's the intended use.
155	has_code_changes() {
156	  local any=0 line path in_artifact dir
157	  while IFS= read -r line; do
158	    [ -z "$line" ] && continue
159	    path="${line:3}"
160	    in_artifact=0
161	    for dir in "${ARTIFACT_DIRS[@]}"; do
162	      case "$path" in
163	        "$dir"/*) in_artifact=1; break ;;
164	      esac
165	    done
166	    [ "$in_artifact" = "0" ] && any=1
167	  done < <(git -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain=v1 2>/dev/null)
168	  [ "$any" = "1" ]
169	}
170	
171	if [ "${#CANDIDATES[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
172	  if has_code_changes; then
173	    log "No agent artifacts to stage; code changes present — nothing to do."
174	    exit 0
175	  fi
176	  log "Nothing to stage: no code changes and no dirty artifacts."
177	  exit 3
178	fi
179	
180	if [ "$ALLOW_EMPTY" = "0" ] && ! has_code_changes; then
181	  log "Refusing: artifacts are dirty but no code changes staged."
182	  log "         A transcript/plan commit without a feature diff is usually wrong."
183	  log "         Re-run with --allow-empty if you really want to commit artifacts alone."
184	  exit 4
185	fi
186	
187	# Stage (or print).
188	for f in "${CANDIDATES[@]}"; do
189	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
190	    printf '[dry-run] would git add: %s\n' "$f"
191	  else
192	    git add -- "$f"
193	    printf 'staged: %s\n' "$f"
194	  fi
195	  STAGED_COUNT=$((STAGED_COUNT + 1))

263	      printf '\n' >> "$file"

265	    printf '\n' >> "$file"

311	#    Skipped if `core.hooksPath` is set globally (chezmoi pattern) — the
312	#    global hook wrapper already runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` for us.

323	  local hooks_path

328	    log "  the repo's .pre-commit-config.yaml automatically."
329	    log "  To use per-repo hooks instead, run: git config --unset core.hooksPath"
330	    return 0
331	  fi
332	
333	  if command -v pre-commit >/dev/null 2>&1; then
334	    pre-commit install
335	    return 0
336	  fi
337	  if command -v uvx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
338	    log "pre-commit not found — using uvx fallback"

341	  fi
342	  warn "neither pre-commit nor uvx available; install pre-commit manually"

5	
6	# agent-history-hygiene
7	
8	Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
9	code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
10	`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.
11	
12	Surfaces, separated by purpose:
13	
14	| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
15	|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
16	| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
17	| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
18	| `agent-commit-metadata.sh`       | "Which harness/model + artifact trailers belong in it?"      |
19	| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
20	| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
21	| `probe-specstory-redaction.py`   | "What does SpecStory already redact, so we don't redo it?"   |
22	| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |
23	
24	## Core invariants
25	
26	1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
27	   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
28	   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
29	2. **SpecStory state is not review history.** Precisely ignore
30	   `.specstory/.project.json` (machine/path-derived identity) and
31	   `.specstory/statistics.json` (regenerable statistics), but never ignore
32	   `.specstory/` or `.specstory/history/` as a whole.
33	3. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
34	   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
35	   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
36	4. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
37	   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
38	   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
39	   history back.
40	4. **Provenance is derived from the staged snapshot.** Never point a commit
41	   trailer at an unstaged transcript/plan, and never guess an unknown model.
42	
43	## When to use this skill
44	
45	Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:
46	
47	- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
48	  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
49	- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
50	  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
51	  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
52	- You see recurring `.specstory/.project.json` or
53	  `.specstory/statistics.json` churn, especially across machines.
54	- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
55	  chat history".
56	- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how

59	  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and

61	
62	## When NOT to use

64	- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
65	  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and

104	## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene

107	chat/plan artifacts.

111	#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.

114	# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.

118	# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.

137	## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project
138	
139	For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`

143	cd /path/to/new/project
144	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \

151	What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:
152	
153	1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
154	   (skips if already present unless `--force`). The redactor is a pinned
155	   remote hook (`repo: …/agent-skills`, `rev: ahh-v1.1.0`), **not** a
156	   vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py` — so `pre-commit autoupdate`

162	   /statistics.json

166	   without hiding `.specstory/history/`. If either state file is already
167	   tracked, bootstrap warns because ignore rules do not affect tracked files;

169	   keeping the local files on disk. Use `--dry-run` to preview it.

179	   configured, bootstrap fails before writing anything: `.git/hooks/` would be

181	   or unset that override for the repo.

186	```bash
187	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
188	```
189	
190	removes the vendored script and rewrites the local hook into the pinned
191	remote hook, leaving your other hooks and `.gitleaks.toml` untouched
192	(idempotent; safe to re-run).

194	## Workflow C: post-leak remediation
195	
196	When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
197	committed / pushed a secret":
198	
199	1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
200	2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
201	3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
202	   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
203	   become worth discussing.
204	4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.
205	
206	## Gotchas
207	
208	- **`.gitignore` does not retroactively untrack files.** SpecStory's own
209	  nested ignore historically covered `.project.json` but not the later-added
210	  `statistics.json`, and either file may already be committed. Adding the two
211	  precise rules stops new files only. Run bootstrap with
212	  `--untrack-specstory-state` to stage their removal from Git while preserving
213	  both local files. Never compensate with `.specstory/` or
214	  `.specstory/history/` in an ignore file; that discards the review trail.
215	- **SpecStory >= 2.4.0 already redacts on write — plan around it, not
216	  against it.** Since
217	  [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) shipped in
218	  v2.4.0 (2026-07-20), the CLI redacts secrets via the
219	  [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset **by
220	  default**, covering both local markdown and cloud sync, writing
221	  `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`. Measured coverage is 36 of 54 class/context pairs;
222	  15 are ours alone (every webhook rule, plus every custom key in prose
223	  context — betterleaks catches many classes only in `KEY=value` form via its
224	  entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule). So: **keep this layer, but never
225	  rewrite what SpecStory already cleaned.** `redact_secrets.py` writes the
226	  same `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` sentinel and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, so
227	  a cleaned transcript is left untouched and pre-commit stops demanding a
228	  re-`git add`. Full matrix + knobs in
229	  [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md).
230	  Only `[redaction] enabled` is configurable upstream — the PR's
231	  `extra_patterns` did not survive the Betterleaks rewrite, so repo-specific
232	  rules stay our job. For SpecStory older than 2.4.0 (or with redaction
233	  disabled), run `redact_secrets.py --fix --legacy`.
234	- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
235	  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
236	  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
237	  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
238	  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
239	  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
240	  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
241	- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
242	  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
243	  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
244	  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
245	  syntax everywhere.
246	- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
247	  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
248	  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
249	- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
250	  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
251	  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
252	  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
253	  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
254	- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
255	  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
256	  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
257	  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
258	  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
259	  `find-session.sh`.
260	- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
261	  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
262	  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
263	  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
264	  agent artifacts, not after.
265	- **`--install-hook` cannot bypass `core.hooksPath`.** Git reads hooks from the
266	  configured directory instead of `.git/hooks/`; writing a repo-local
267	  `prepare-commit-msg` there would silently do nothing. Bootstrap now exits 6
268	  before creating files and prints the two valid remedies. It never edits a
269	  user's global hook directory on their behalf.
270	- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
271	  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
272	  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
273	  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
274	  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
275	  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
276	  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
277	  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
278	  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
279	  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
280	  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
281	  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
282	  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
283	  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
284	  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
285	  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
286	  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
287	  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
288	  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
289	  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
290	  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.
291	  **Fixed sub-case:** the *bare-phrase* variant of this loop — where the
292	  redactor's own `PRIVATE KEY` substring match kept flagging prose that
293	  merely *discusses* private keys (this skill's docs, or a chat about
294	  redaction) with **no real secret present** — no longer happens.
295	  `redact_secrets.py` now scopes to key *headers* (the
296	  `detect-private-key` BLACKLIST), so prose mentions are ignored and
297	  converge immediately. The atomic-commit workaround above is still
298	  needed for the harder case: a **real** secret an active writer keeps
299	  re-appending. When only the substring redactor (`redact-agent-secrets`)
300	  trips while `gitleaks` + `detect-private-key` pass, it's the false
301	  positive — verify with `gitleaks git --staged` and, if clean, commit
302	  with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` (keeps the real gates active).
303	
304	## Available scripts
305	
306	- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
307	  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
308	  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
309	  empty fields signal absence).
310	
311	- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
312	  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
313	  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
314	  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
315	  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
316	  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.
317	
318	- **`scripts/agent-commit-metadata.sh [--harness NAME --model NAME] [--format trailers|json]`**
319	  Read staged SpecStory/plan artifacts and emit deduplicated
320	  `AI-Assisted-By`, `Agent-Transcript`, and `Agent-Plan` values. Parses the
321	  staged blob rather than a concurrently-changing working-tree transcript;
322	  requires explicit harness+model overrides when it cannot prove them.
323	
324	- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
325	  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
326	  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
327	  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.
328	
329	- **`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py [--json] [--keep] [--dry-run]`**
330	  Measure which secret classes SpecStory's native redaction covers, by
331	  synthesizing a Claude Code session and rendering it twice (with and without
332	  `--no-redact-secrets`). Prints a coverage matrix and the residual set our
333	  layer must still handle. Exit 30 when specstory isn't installed.
334	
335	- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--migrate] [--install-hook] [--untrack-specstory-state] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
336	  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the current
337	  repo, merge precise SpecStory state ignores, wire the hook to the installed
338	  skill's redactor, then run `pre-commit install`. Audits
339	  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
340	  without hiding transcript directories. Already-tracked state is only
341	  untracked with the explicit flag; `--dry-run` previews that index change.
342	  `--install-hook` exits 6 when `core.hooksPath` would make the repo-local
343	  hook inert.

```text
1	# Transcript & session discovery
2	
3	How `find-session.sh` locates "the session you are in right now" across
4	the fragmented landscape of coding-agent artifacts.
5	
6	## The core problem
7	
8	Several agents can be running in parallel against the same repository —
9	one Claude Code window, a background subagent, a Cursor window, plus
10	VS Code with the SpecStory extension auto-saving. Each writes into its
11	own directory using its own naming convention. There is no canonical
12	"current session" pointer; the best you can do is pick the freshest
13	artifact tied to `$PWD` and verify.
14	
15	## Claude Code session layout
16	
17	Claude Code stores each session as a JSON-lines file inside a
18	project-scoped directory:
19	
20	```
21	~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session-uuid>.jsonl
22	```
23	
24	The slug is the absolute working directory with **every non-alphanumeric
25	character** replaced by `-`, not just `/`. For
26	`$PWD=/Volumes/Data/Program/Personal/agent-skills` the slug is
27	`-Volumes-Data-Program-Personal-agent-skills` (leading dash included). A dot or
28	underscore collapses the same way, which is easy to miss:
29	`/home/<user>/.local/share/chezmoi` is stored as
30	`-home-<user>--local-share-chezmoi` — the dot becomes the second dash. Rebuild
31	the slug with `sed 's/[^A-Za-z0-9]/-/g'`, not `tr '/' '-'`, or a path
32	containing `.`/`_`/space silently resolves to a directory that doesn't exist
33	(`specstory sync` then reports `1 session not found`). The UUID is the Claude
34	session ID surfaced in `/status`.
35	
36	Heuristic: **the newest `.jsonl` in that directory is the active
37	session's transcript.** This breaks if you spawn a subagent that writes
38	into the same project dir and then stop interacting with the parent — the
39	subagent's JSONL wins by mtime. In practice the user knows which session
40	they're working in; the heuristic is fine for the "commit my chat" flow.
41	
42	## SpecStory history layout
43	
44	SpecStory writes one Markdown file per conversation:
45	
46	```
47	<repo-root>/.specstory/history/<timestamp>.md
48	```
49	
50	The timestamp is UTC ISO-8601-ish (e.g. `2026-04-24_05-05-10Z.md`). The
51	VS Code extension auto-saves continuously (controlled by
52	`specstory.autoSave`) so the file grows during the conversation. The CLI
53	(`specstory run claude`, `specstory sync claude -s <uuid>`) emits a new
54	file per session explicitly.
55	
56	Heuristic: **the newest `.md` in `.specstory/history/` is the active
57	transcript.** Same caveat as Claude — parallel sessions produce multiple
58	fresh files; mtime wins.
59	
60	## `find-session.sh` output shape
61	
62	TSV by default (two columns per line, tab-separated):
63	
64	```
65	specstory_path      <abs path or empty>
66	claude_session_uuid <uuid or empty>
67	claude_jsonl_path   <abs path or empty>
68	```
69	
70	`--json` emits a single-line JSON object. The script NEVER fails (always
71	exits 0) so agents can pipe it into downstream commands without
72	`set -e` explosions when a session isn't present.
73	
74	## When the heuristic breaks
75	
76	1. **Multiple concurrent agents in the same repo.** If you care which is
77	   "yours", open the session picker in your IDE (Claude Code's `/status`;
78	   SpecStory's session list) and grep for the UUID directly.
79	2. **Subagent writes a newer file than the parent.** After a long
80	   subagent run, the parent session's JSONL may look stale. The
81	   `--format=specstory` and `--format=claude` flags let you isolate one
82	   dimension.
83	3. **Repository renamed on disk.** Claude's slug is frozen at session
84	   start — if you `mv` the repo mid-session, the slug stops matching
85	   `$PWD`. Restart the agent to get a fresh session/slug pair.
86	4. **Worktrees.** `git worktree` directories have their own `$PWD` and
87	   thus their own slug. SpecStory stores per-worktree history too (it
88	   keys off `.specstory/history/` inside each worktree root).
89	
90	## SpecStory CLI integration (optional)
91	
92	If the user runs `specstory` directly:
93	
94	```bash
95	# Start a wrapped Claude Code session that auto-logs into .specstory/history/
96	specstory run claude
97	
98	# Sync a specific Claude session's JSONL into SpecStory's Markdown format
99	specstory sync claude -s <uuid>
100	
101	# List Claude sessions SpecStory knows about
102	specstory list claude
103	```
104	
105	When the VS Code extension is the source of truth (most common), the CLI
106	commands are unnecessary — the extension already wrote the file. Only
107	use `specstory sync` when you want to force-refresh a transcript for a
108	session whose files haven't auto-saved.
109	
110	## Cross-reference
111	
112	- [`pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](./pre-commit-redaction-stack.md) —
113	  how the located session files get scanned / redacted at commit time.
114	- [`../scripts/find-session.sh`](../scripts/find-session.sh) — the
115	  script implementing these heuristics.
116	- [`../scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh`](../scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh)
117	  — the caller that uses `find-session.sh --format=specstory` to locate
118	  the current transcript for `--session-only` staging.
119
```

26	dim()   { printf '\033[2m%s\033[0m' "$*"; }
27	
28	pass() {
29	  PASS_COUNT=$((PASS_COUNT + 1))
30	  printf '  %s %s\n' "$(green PASS)" "$1"
31	}
32	fail() {
33	  FAIL_COUNT=$((FAIL_COUNT + 1))
34	  printf '  %s %s\n' "$(red FAIL)" "$1"
35	  FAIL_LOG="${FAIL_LOG}FAIL: $1\n"
36	}
37	
38	# make_repo — spin up an isolated tmp repo with an initial commit.

51	# (byte-identical to the fixture otherwise). Line-based sed → newline never
52	# enters the pattern space, so [[:space:]]* only eats the horizontal separator.
53	stage_fixture() {

55	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$repo/$dest_rel")"

14	## Layout
15	
16	- `fixtures/` — paired `.md` files exercising gitleaks rules + allowlist.
17	  Each filename encodes its expected behavior (e.g. `real_anthropic.md`
18	  should fire, `example_shapes.md` should be allowlisted when staged
19	  inside an agent-artifact directory).
20	- `conftest.py` — shared pytest fixtures; loads the PEP 723 script
21	  `assets/redact_secrets.py` as an importable module.
22	- `test_redact_secrets.py` — unit tests for pure functions in the
23	  redactor (`redact_secret`, `filter_by_prefixes`,
24	  `find_private_key_files`, `redact_file`, `redact_private_keys`).
25	- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus tests: stages each fixture
26	  in a throwaway git repo and asserts `gitleaks git --staged` returns
27	  the expected findings (or lack thereof). Skipped if `gitleaks` is
28	  not on `PATH`.
29	- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
30	  `scripts/scan-staged.sh`: `0` clean, `20` leak, `30` missing
31	  gitleaks, `2` not a git repo.
32	- `test_bootstrap_project.py` — verifies precise, idempotent nested SpecStory
33	  ignores; confirms `history/` stays visible; checks dry-run and the explicit
34	  `--untrack-specstory-state` migration contract.
35	
36	## Test-vector hygiene (why the fixtures carry `gitleaks:allow`)
37	
38	The firing fixtures (`real_anthropic.md`, `real_openai.md`, `private_key.md`,
39	`webhook_urls.md`) hold deliberately-fake test vectors. Most use realistic
40	secret shapes plus an inline marker so a repo-root, downstream, or
41	`npx skills add`-installed gitleaks scan **skips them by default**:
42	
43	```
44	<SECRET> <!-- gitleaks:allow -->                      # markdown fixtures
45	"-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\n"  # gitleaks:allow  # test_redact_secrets.py
46	```
47	
48	The Stripe webhook fixture is stricter: GitHub's provider-level scanner does
49	not honour gitleaks markers, so its source uses
50	`__SYNTHETIC_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET__`. The corpus test expands that placeholder
51	inside its throwaway repo. The other corpus + shell tests **strip the marker
52	before staging** (`_GITLEAKS_MARKER_RE` in `test_gitleaks_corpus.py`; the `sed`
53	in `stage_fixture` in `test_scan_staged.sh`), so the secret bytes have the exact
54	shape the rules expect and the assertions still fire. Principle: **fake test
55	vectors are out of scan scope by default, and only "fire" when a test re-plants
56	them.**
57	
58	Invariant — **the strip must be byte-identical**: never change a secret's length
59	or the length-sensitive rules (`sk-proj-…{80,}`, `sk-ant-api\d{2}-…{93}AA`, the
60	webhook regexes) stop matching. When adding a new firing fixture, append the
61	marker with a single leading space (`<SECRET> <!-- gitleaks:allow -->`); the
62	strip regex reclaims exactly that separator. `clean.md` / `example_shapes.md`
63	carry no marker (the strip is a no-op) and must keep their must-not-fire
64	behavior. GitHub-native secret scanning ignores the marker; it's excluded
65	separately via the repo's `.github/secret_scanning.yml`. This replaced a former
66	repo-root `.gitleaksignore` whose `file:rule:line` fingerprints silently drifted.
67
